Fix an integer $d\ge2$. Let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected open domain with $C^\infty$ boundary, and let $\Omega'\subset\Omega$ be an open domain whose closure is compact and contained in $\Omega$. Fix real parameters $m>0$, $M\ge\max\{1,m\}$, $R>0$, and $0<\alpha<1$. Define
$$\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega):=\{\gamma\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R):m\le\gamma(x)\le M\text{ for almost every }x\in\Omega\}$$
and
$$\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega'):=\{\gamma\in\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega):\gamma=1\text{ almost everywhere on }\Omega\setminus\Omega'\}.$$
For $\gamma\in BV(\Omega)$ set $\|\gamma\|_{BV(\Omega)}:=\max\{\|\gamma\|_{L^1(\Omega)},TV(\gamma;\Omega)\}$. For a continuously differentiable function on $\overline\Omega$ whose first derivatives are $\alpha$-Hölder continuous, set
$$\|\gamma\|_{C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\max\left\{\max_{|\beta|\le1}\sup_{x\in\overline\Omega}|\partial^\beta\gamma(x)|,\ \max_{|\beta|=1}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|\partial^\beta\gamma(x)-\partial^\beta\gamma(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}\right\}.$$
Define
$$X_d(R):=\begin{cases}\{\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')\cap BV(\Omega):\|\gamma\|_{BV(\Omega)}\le R\},&d=2,\\[2mm]\{\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')\cap C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega):\|\gamma\|_{C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le R\},&d\ge3.\end{cases}$$
For $\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')$, define its measurable background extension $\gamma_e:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ by $\gamma_e=\gamma$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$ and $\gamma_e=1$ on $\mathbb R^d\setminus\Omega$. Then $\gamma_e-1$ vanishes almost everywhere outside $\Omega'$. No pointwise continuity of $\gamma_e$ is asserted. The classes $X_d(R)$ are not assumed nonempty.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected smooth domain, and let $\gamma\in\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega)$ be a real almost-everywhere class with $0<m\le\gamma\le M<\infty$. Set $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ with quotient norm $\|[U]\|_{\mathcal D}:=\inf_{w\in H_0^1(\Omega)}\|U+w\|_{H^1(\Omega)}$, and let $\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$ be its continuous conjugate-linear dual. For $f=[U]\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, let $u_{\gamma,f}$ be the unique element of the coset $f$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla z}\,dx=0\qquad(z\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)).$$
Define the weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann map $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$ by
$$\bigl(\Lambda_\gamma f\bigr)(g):=\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla V_g}\,dx,$$
where $V_g$ is any representative of $g\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$. The trace quotient identification makes $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ the $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ boundary data space with its trace quotient norm. Constants lie in the kernel of $\Lambda_\gamma$, and its range functionals annihilate constants; hence $\Lambda_\gamma$ induces $\dot\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1\to(\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1)^*$, the quotient Dirichlet-to-Neumann map used for Calderón stability. Well-posedness, independence from the representative $V_g$, boundedness and the induced quotient map are established by the well-posedness result cited below.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected $C^1$ domain, let $0<m\le M<\infty$, and let $\gamma\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $m\le\gamma\le M$ almost everywhere. Define $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ with its quotient norm. For every boundary trace class $f\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ there is a unique $u_{\gamma,f}\in f$ such that
$$\int_\Omega\gamma\,
abla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{
abla z}\,dx=0\qquad	ext{for every }z\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C).$$
For every $g\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, the value $\int_\Omega\gamma
abla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{
abla V_g}\,dx$ is independent of the representative $V_g\in g$ and defines a bounded linear map $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)	o\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$. Constants are in its kernel and its range functionals annihilate constants.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n\ge1$
and let $e_k(x)=\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot x)$, $k\in\mathbb Z^n$, be the coordinate
characters on $\mathbb T^n$
([[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]],
[[def-fourier-coefficients-and-trigonometric-polynomials]]). Then:

1. $(e_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^n}$ is an orthonormal family in the complex Hilbert
   space $L^2(\mathbb T^n)$;
2. it is an orthonormal basis: its closed linear span is $L^2(\mathbb T^n)$;
3. consequently the Fourier expansion
   $f=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^n}\widehat f(k)e_k$ and Parseval's identity
   $$\|f\|_2^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^n}|\widehat f(k)|^2,\qquad \langle f,g\rangle=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^n}\widehat f(k)\overline{\widehat g(k)}$$
   hold for all $f,g\in L^2(\mathbb T^n)$, in the finite-subset-net sense; and
4. the Fourier coefficient map is a surjective linear isometry of
   $L^2(\mathbb T^n)$ onto $\ell^2(\mathbb Z^n,\mathbb C)$.

No Hilbert tensor-product identification is used anywhere.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a
bounded $C^1$ domain, $1<p<\infty$, $p'=p/(p-1)$,
$u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, $v\in W^{1,p'}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and let
$T$ be the trace of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] with
$\nu$ the outward normal of
[[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]. Then for
every $i=1,\dots,n$,
$$\int_\Omega u\,\partial_iv\,dx=-\int_\Omega(\partial_iu)v\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega}(Tu)(Tv)\,\nu_i\,dS,$$
and all three integrals are finite. If $u,v\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$, the
boundary term is the classical $\int_{\partial\Omega}uv\,\nu_i\,dS$ of the
divergence theorem
[[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]] applied to the
field $uv\,e_i$; if in addition $Tu=\partial_\nu w$ on $\partial\Omega$ for a specified $w\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$, the boundary term is $\int_{\partial\Omega}(\partial_\nu w)(Tv)\nu_i\,dS$. The normal derivative of [[def-classical-normal-derivative]] is defined on the boundary, and this extra identity is an assumption, not an interior substitution.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected smooth domain, and let $\gamma\in\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega)$ be a real almost-everywhere class with $0<m\le\gamma\le M<\infty$. Set $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ with quotient norm $\|[U]\|_{\mathcal D}:=\inf_{w\in H_0^1(\Omega)}\|U+w\|_{H^1(\Omega)}$, and let $\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$ be its continuous conjugate-linear dual. For $f=[U]\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, let $u_{\gamma,f}$ be the unique element of the coset $f$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla z}\,dx=0\qquad(z\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)).$$
Define the weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann map $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$ by
$$\bigl(\Lambda_\gamma f\bigr)(g):=\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla V_g}\,dx,$$
where $V_g$ is any representative of $g\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$. The trace quotient identification makes $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ the $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ boundary data space with its trace quotient norm. Constants lie in the kernel of $\Lambda_\gamma$, and its range functionals annihilate constants; hence $\Lambda_\gamma$ induces $\dot\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1\to(\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1)^*$, the quotient Dirichlet-to-Neumann map used for Calderón stability. Well-posedness, independence from the representative $V_g$, boundedness and the induced quotient map are established by the well-posedness result cited below.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $n\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty bounded connected open set whose boundary is covered by finitely many $C^1$ graph charts. Give $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ its Sobolev norm, let $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ be the $H^1$-closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and let $W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ have the finite-chart Slobodeckij norm. Define $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with its quotient norm. The trace induces a bounded linear bijection $\overline T:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with bounded inverse, so these two norms are equivalent under the induced identification. The induced map after quotienting by constants is also a bounded linear bijection $\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb K\mathbf1\to W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)/\mathbb K$, with equivalent quotient norms. A continuous linear functional on $W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ descends to the constant quotient exactly when it annihilates constants, and its descended functional has the quotient dual norm.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k\ge1$, $1\le p<\infty$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a
bounded $C^k$ domain in the graph sense of
[[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]. Then the set of restrictions
to $\Omega$ of functions in $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$ is dense in
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$: for every $u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and
every $\delta>0$ there is $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|\varphi|_\Omega-u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$.

The exponent range is $1\le p<\infty$; the result asserts no density in the
$W^{k,\infty}$ norm, and it does not hold on arbitrary open sets, as the
companion examples page shows.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. Let $f_n:X\to[0,+\infty]$ be measurable for every $n\ge1$, with $0\le f_1\le f_2\le\cdots$, and suppose $f_n(x)\uparrow f(x)$ for every $x\in X$. Then
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\uparrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

Assume Countable Choice, as in
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and
[[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]]. For an open set
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge1$, an integer $k\ge0$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, set
$$H^k(\Omega;\mathbb K):=W^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The elements are the same almost-everywhere classes, and their weak
derivatives and norm are exactly those already defined for $W^{k,2}$. When the
scalar field is fixed, write $H^k(\Omega)$.

The notation $H^k_0(\Omega)$ is reserved for the later definition by closure of
compactly supported smooth functions in the Sobolev norm. This item assigns no
boundary values to an equivalence class and asserts no characterization by
pointwise vanishing or by traces.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Let $n=|k|$, $s=r/a$, and $\sigma=1+\beta$. In polar coordinates $\rho=|x-x_0|$, seek a solution with angular mode $e^{ik\theta}$, using $u_i=A\rho^ne^{ik\theta}$ for $\rho<r$ and $u_o=(B\rho^n+C\rho^{-n})e^{ik\theta}$ for $r<\rho<a$. Continuity of $u$ and continuity of $\gamma\partial_\rho u$ at $\rho=r$ give $C r^{-2n}=-\eta B$ because $(\sigma-1)/(\sigma+1)=\eta$. The boundary condition $u_o(a,\theta)=e_k(\theta)$ then gives $Ba^n=(1-\eta s^{2n})^{-1}$.

Each piece is harmonic on its subdomain, and its value and conductivity-weighted normal derivative agree at $\rho=r$ by step 1.1. Both pieces and their classical gradients are bounded up to the interface because $r>0$. Testing a distributional first derivative against $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(D)$ and integrating by parts on the inner disk and annulus produces interface terms equal to the jump in $u$ times $\varphi$; the matching values cancel these terms, leaving the bounded piecewise classical derivatives. By [F7] the glued function belongs to $H^1(D)$. For any $z\in C_c^\infty(D)$, integration by parts on the inner disk and outer annulus cancels the interface flux terms and proves the weak equation. Since $C_c^\infty(D)$ is dense in $H_0^1(D)$ by [F1] and the energy form is continuous, the equation holds for every $z\in H_0^1(D)$. By [F1] the function is the unique solution for trace $e_k$. At $\rho=a$, the conductivity is $1$, so the outward flux is
$$\partial_\rho u_o(a,\theta)=\frac{n}{a}\frac{1+\eta s^{2n}}{1-\eta s^{2n}}e_k(\theta).$$
The Gauss–Green identity [F3] identifies this flux with the weak DN functional. For $\gamma_1\equiv1$, the harmonic extension $(\rho/a)^n e_k(\theta)$ gives flux $(n/a)e_k$, and the constant solution has zero flux.

For each angle $\theta$, define $(R_\theta U)(x)=U(x_0+Q_\theta(x-x_0))$ on $D$, where $Q_\theta$ is the planar rotation matrix, and define $P_kU=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}e^{-ik\theta}R_\theta U\,d\theta$. By density [F5] and the rotation isometries, $\theta\mapsto R_\theta U$ is strongly continuous in $H^1(D)$ for every $U$, so this integral is the $H^1$ limit of its Riemann sums. Rotations preserve the $H^1(D)$ inner product; Minkowski's inequality makes $P_k$ a contraction, and character orthogonality [F2] makes it a self-adjoint projection with pairwise orthogonal ranges. For $w\in C_c^\infty(D)$, the map $\theta\mapsto R_\theta w$ is continuous in $H^1$ and every Riemann sum of the displayed integral is in $C_c^\infty(D)$, so $P_kw\in H_0^1(D)$; contraction and density in the definition of $H_0^1$ extend this invariance to all of $H_0^1(D)$. For a smooth restriction $U$, the polar-coordinate chain rule gives the $H^1$ norm as the integral of $|U|^2+|\partial_\rho U|^2+\rho^{-2}|\partial_\theta U|^2$ against $\rho\,d\rho d\theta$. Parseval [F2] for these three terms and monotone convergence [F6] in the radial integral show that the finite orthogonal sums $S_N:=\sum_{|k|\le N}P_k$ converge to $U$ in $H^1(D)$. For a general $U\in H^1(D)$, approximate by smooth restrictions using [F5]; on each annulus $\epsilon<\rho<a$ the polar map is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism, so the polar norm and Fourier identities pass to the limit there, and monotone convergence [F6] as $\epsilon\downarrow0$ gives the full-disk identities. Each $S_N$ is an orthogonal projection and hence a contraction; density [F5] therefore extends $S_NU\to U$ to every $U\in H^1(D)$. The induced quotient modes are thus a complete orthogonal family in $\mathcal D(D)$, and the constant mode is orthogonal to every nonzero mode. Since the trace is bounded and rotation-equivariant on smooth functions, [F4] and [F5] extend commutation to all of $H^1(D)$; the trace-kernel identity in [F4] then shows that each projected boundary class is a scalar multiple of one mode. For any $H^1$ representative $U$ of the boundary mode $e_k$, let $v(\rho)$ be its $k$th angular Fourier coefficient. Parseval gives
$$\|U\|_{H^1(D)}^2\ge 2\pi\int_0^a\left(|v'(\rho)|^2\rho+\frac{n^2|v(\rho)|^2}{\rho}\right)d\rho.$$
The trace condition gives $v(a)=1$. On every interval $[\epsilon,a]$, the one-dimensional Sobolev representative of $v$ is absolutely continuous, and expansion of the square yields
$$\int_\epsilon^a\left(|v'|^2\rho+\frac{n^2|v|^2}{\rho}\right)d\rho=\int_\epsilon^a\left|v'-\frac n\rho v\right|^2\rho\,d\rho+n|v(a)|^2-n|v(\epsilon)|^2.$$
The full energy being finite implies $\int_0^a|v(\rho)|^2\rho^{-1}d\rho<\infty$, so there is a sequence $\epsilon_j\downarrow0$ with $v(\epsilon_j)\to0$; otherwise $|v|$ would be bounded below near zero and this integral would diverge. Letting $\epsilon=\epsilon_j$ and using nonnegativity of the square proves that the radial energy is at least $n$. Thus every representative has squared $H^1$ norm at least $2\pi n$, so [F4] gives $Q_n^{\mathcal D}:=\|e_k\|_{\mathcal D(D)}^2\ge2\pi n$. The harmonic lift $(\rho/a)^ne_k$ has squared $H^1$ norm $2\pi n+\pi a^2/(n+1)$ by direct radial integration, so [F4] gives $Q_n^{\mathcal D}\le2\pi n+\pi a^2/(n+1)$. Orthogonality of the constant mode to $e_k$ gives $\|e_k+c\mathbf1\|_{\mathcal D}^2=Q_n^{\mathcal D}+|c|^2\|\mathbf1\|_{\mathcal D}^2$; the constant class has positive norm by the trace isomorphism [F4]. Taking the infimum over $c$ shows that the statement's further quotient norm satisfies $Q_n=Q_n^{\mathcal D}$.

The weak DN map is diagonal on the complete orthogonal quotient modes from step 2.1; the constant mode is orthogonal to all nonzero modes, so quotienting by constants leaves $Q_n$ unchanged: angular integration makes the pairing of mode $e_k$ with any distinct mode zero, and step 1.2 gives its diagonal coefficient. For finite sums, the dual norm of the difference applied to $\sum a_ke_k$ is $\bigl(\sum_{k\ne0}|a_k|^2(2\pi a|\lambda_n(r)-n/a|)^2/Q_n\bigr)^{1/2}$; boundedness [F1] and density extend this formula to all inputs. Therefore
$$\|\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_r}-\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_1}\|=\sup_{k\ne0}\frac{2\pi a\,|\lambda_n(r)-n/a|}{Q_n},\qquad \lambda_n(r)-\frac na=\frac{2n}{a}\frac{\eta s^{2n}}{1-\eta s^{2n}}.$$
Using $Q_n\ge2\pi n$, $0<s\le1/2$, and $0<\eta<1$, this is at most
$$\sup_{n\ge1}\frac{2\eta s^{2n}}{1-\eta s^{2n}}\le\frac{2\eta}{1-\eta}s^2.$$
This proves all asserted eigenvalue and operator-norm formulas.

Fix an integer $d\ge2$. Let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected open domain with $C^\infty$ boundary, and let $\Omega'\subset\Omega$ be an open domain whose closure is compact and contained in $\Omega$. Fix real parameters $m>0$, $M\ge\max\{1,m\}$, $R>0$, and $0<\alpha<1$. Define
$$\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega):=\{\gamma\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R):m\le\gamma(x)\le M\text{ for almost every }x\in\Omega\}$$
and
$$\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega'):=\{\gamma\in\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega):\gamma=1\text{ almost everywhere on }\Omega\setminus\Omega'\}.$$
For $\gamma\in BV(\Omega)$ set $\|\gamma\|_{BV(\Omega)}:=\max\{\|\gamma\|_{L^1(\Omega)},TV(\gamma;\Omega)\}$. For a continuously differentiable function on $\overline\Omega$ whose first derivatives are $\alpha$-Hölder continuous, set
$$\|\gamma\|_{C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\max\left\{\max_{|\beta|\le1}\sup_{x\in\overline\Omega}|\partial^\beta\gamma(x)|,\ \max_{|\beta|=1}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|\partial^\beta\gamma(x)-\partial^\beta\gamma(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}\right\}.$$
Define
$$X_d(R):=\begin{cases}\{\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')\cap BV(\Omega):\|\gamma\|_{BV(\Omega)}\le R\},&d=2,\\[2mm]\{\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')\cap C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega):\|\gamma\|_{C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le R\},&d\ge3.\end{cases}$$
For $\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')$, define its measurable background extension $\gamma_e:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ by $\gamma_e=\gamma$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$ and $\gamma_e=1$ on $\mathbb R^d\setminus\Omega$. Then $\gamma_e-1$ vanishes almost everywhere outside $\Omega'$. No pointwise continuity of $\gamma_e$ is asserted. The classes $X_d(R)$ are not assumed nonempty.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> (Choice function).

there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.

countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Let $n=|k|$, $s=r/a$, and $\sigma=1+\beta$. In polar coordinates $\rho=|x-x_0|$, seek a solution with angular mode $e^{ik\theta}$, using $u_i=A\rho^ne^{ik\theta}$ for $\rho<r$ and $u_o=(B\rho^n+C\rho^{-n})e^{ik\theta}$ for $r<\rho<a$. Continuity of $u$ and continuity of $\gamma\partial_\rho u$ at $\rho=r$ give $C r^{-2n}=-\eta B$ because $(\sigma-1)/(\sigma+1)=\eta$. The boundary condition $u_o(a,\theta)=e_k(\theta)$ then gives $Ba^n=(1-\eta s^{2n})^{-1}$.

Each piece is harmonic on its subdomain, and its value and conductivity-weighted normal derivative agree at $\rho=r$ by step 1.1. Both pieces and their classical gradients are bounded up to the interface because $r>0$. Testing a distributional first derivative against $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(D)$ and integrating by parts on the inner disk and annulus produces interface terms equal to the jump in $u$ times $\varphi$; the matching values cancel these terms, leaving the bounded piecewise classical derivatives. By [F7] the glued function belongs to $H^1(D)$. For any $z\in C_c^\infty(D)$, integration by parts on the inner disk and outer annulus cancels the interface flux terms and proves the weak equation. Since $C_c^\infty(D)$ is dense in $H_0^1(D)$ by [F1] and the energy form is continuous, the equation holds for every $z\in H_0^1(D)$. By [F1] the function is the unique solution for trace $e_k$. At $\rho=a$, the conductivity is $1$, so the outward flux is $$\partial_\rho u_o(a,\theta)=\frac{n}{a}\frac{1+\eta s^{2n}}{1-\eta s^{2n}}e_k(\theta).$$ The Gauss–Green identity [F3] identifies this flux with the weak DN functional. For $\gamma_1\equiv1$, the harmonic extension $(\rho/a)^n e_k(\theta)$ gives flux $(n/a)e_k$, and the constant solution has zero flux.

For each angle $\theta$, define $(R_\theta U)(x)=U(x_0+Q_\theta(x-x_0))$ on $D$, where $Q_\theta$ is the planar rotation matrix, and define $P_kU=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}e^{-ik\theta}R_\theta U\,d\theta$. By density [F5] and the rotation isometries, $\theta\mapsto R_\theta U$ is strongly continuous in $H^1(D)$ for every $U$, so this integral is the $H^1$ limit of its Riemann sums. Rotations preserve the $H^1(D)$ inner product; Minkowski's inequality makes $P_k$ a contraction, and character orthogonality [F2] makes it a self-adjoint projection with pairwise orthogonal ranges. For $w\in C_c^\infty(D)$, the map $\theta\mapsto R_\theta w$ is continuous in $H^1$ and every Riemann sum of the displayed integral is in $C_c^\infty(D)$, so $P_kw\in H_0^1(D)$; contraction and density in the definition of $H_0^1$ extend this invariance to all of $H_0^1(D)$. For a smooth restriction $U$, the polar-coordinate chain rule gives the $H^1$ norm as the integral of $|U|^2+|\partial_\rho U|^2+\rho^{-2}|\partial_\theta U|^2$ against $\rho\,d\rho d\theta$. Parseval [F2] for these three terms and monotone convergence [F6] in the radial integral show that the finite orthogonal sums $S_N:=\sum_{|k|\le N}P_k$ converge to $U$ in $H^1(D)$. For a general $U\in H^1(D)$, approximate by smooth restrictions using [F5]; on each annulus $\epsilon<\rho<a$ the polar map is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism, so the polar norm and Fourier identities pass to the limit there, and monotone convergence [F6] as $\epsilon\downarrow0$ gives the full-disk identities. Each $S_N$ is an orthogonal projection and hence a contraction; density [F5] therefore extends $S_NU\to U$ to every $U\in H^1(D)$. The induced quotient modes are thus a complete orthogonal family in $\mathcal D(D)$, and the constant mode is orthogonal to every nonzero mode. Since the trace is bounded and rotation-equivariant on smooth functions, [F4] and [F5] extend commutation to all of $H^1(D)$; the trace-kernel identity in [F4] then shows that each projected boundary class is a scalar multiple of one mode. For any $H^1$ representative $U$ of the boundary mode $e_k$, let $v(\rho)$ be its $k$th angular Fourier coefficient. Parseval gives $$\|U\|_{H^1(D)}^2\ge 2\pi\int_0^a\left(|v'(\rho)|^2\rho+\frac{n^2|v(\rho)|^2}{\rho}\right)d\rho.$$ The trace condition gives $v(a)=1$. On every interval $[\epsilon,a]$, the one-dimensional Sobolev representative of $v$ is absolutely continuous, and expansion of the square yields $$\int_\epsilon^a\left(|v'|^2\rho+\frac{n^2|v|^2}{\rho}\right)d\rho=\int_\epsilon^a\left|v'-\frac n\rho v\right|^2\rho\,d\rho+n|v(a)|^2-n|v(\epsilon)|^2.$$ The full energy being finite implies $\int_0^a|v(\rho)|^2\rho^{-1}d\rho<\infty$, so there is a sequence $\epsilon_j\downarrow0$ with $v(\epsilon_j)\to0$; otherwise $|v|$ would be bounded below near zero and this integral would diverge. Letting $\epsilon=\epsilon_j$ and using nonnegativity of the square proves that the radial energy is at least $n$. Thus every representative has squared $H^1$ norm at least $2\pi n$, so [F4] gives $Q_n^{\mathcal D}:=\|e_k\|_{\mathcal D(D)}^2\ge2\pi n$. The harmonic lift $(\rho/a)^ne_k$ has squared $H^1$ norm $2\pi n+\pi a^2/(n+1)$ by direct radial integration, so [F4] gives $Q_n^{\mathcal D}\le2\pi n+\pi a^2/(n+1)$. Orthogonality of the constant mode to $e_k$ gives $\|e_k+c\mathbf1\|_{\mathcal D}^2=Q_n^{\mathcal D}+|c|^2\|\mathbf1\|_{\mathcal D}^2$; the constant class has positive norm by the trace isomorphism [F4]. Taking the infimum over $c$ shows that the statement's further quotient norm satisfies $Q_n=Q_n^{\mathcal D}$.

The weak DN map is diagonal on the complete orthogonal quotient modes from step 3.1; the constant mode is orthogonal to all nonzero modes, so quotienting by constants leaves $Q_n$ unchanged: angular integration makes the pairing of mode $e_k$ with any distinct mode zero, and step 2.1 gives its diagonal coefficient. For finite sums, the dual norm of the difference applied to $\sum a_ke_k$ is $\bigl(\sum_{k\ne0}|a_k|^2(2\pi a|\lambda_n(r)-n/a|)^2/Q_n\bigr)^{1/2}$; boundedness [F1] and density extend this formula to all inputs. Therefore $$\|\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_r}-\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_1}\|=\sup_{k\ne0}\frac{2\pi a\,|\lambda_n(r)-n/a|}{Q_n},\qquad \lambda_n(r)-\frac na=\frac{2n}{a}\frac{\eta s^{2n}}{1-\eta s^{2n}}.$$ Using $Q_n\ge2\pi n$, $0<s\le1/2$, and $0<\eta<1$, this is at most $$\sup_{n\ge1}\frac{2\eta s^{2n}}{1-\eta s^{2n}}\le\frac{2\eta}{1-\eta}s^2.$$ This proves all asserted eigenvalue and operator-norm formulas.

Fix an integer $d\ge2$. Let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected open domain with $C^\infty$ boundary, and let $\Omega'\subset\Omega$ be an open domain whose closure is compact and contained in $\Omega$. Fix real parameters $m>0$, $M\ge\max\{1,m\}$, $R>0$, and $0<\alpha<1$. Define
$$\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega):=\{\gamma\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R):m\le\gamma(x)\le M\text{ for almost every }x\in\Omega\}$$
and
$$\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega'):=\{\gamma\in\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega):\gamma=1\text{ almost everywhere on }\Omega\setminus\Omega'\}.$$
For $\gamma\in BV(\Omega)$ set $\|\gamma\|_{BV(\Omega)}:=\max\{\|\gamma\|_{L^1(\Omega)},TV(\gamma;\Omega)\}$. For a continuously differentiable function on $\overline\Omega$ whose first derivatives are $\alpha$-Hölder continuous, set
$$\|\gamma\|_{C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\max\left\{\max_{|\beta|\le1}\sup_{x\in\overline\Omega}|\partial^\beta\gamma(x)|,\ \max_{|\beta|=1}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|\partial^\beta\gamma(x)-\partial^\beta\gamma(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}\right\}.$$
Define
$$X_d(R):=\begin{cases}\{\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')\cap BV(\Omega):\|\gamma\|_{BV(\Omega)}\le R\},&d=2,\\[2mm]\{\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')\cap C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega):\|\gamma\|_{C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le R\},&d\ge3.\end{cases}$$
For $\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')$, define its measurable background extension $\gamma_e:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ by $\gamma_e=\gamma$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$ and $\gamma_e=1$ on $\mathbb R^d\setminus\Omega$. Then $\gamma_e-1$ vanishes almost everywhere outside $\Omega'$. No pointwise continuity of $\gamma_e$ is asserted. The classes $X_d(R)$ are not assumed nonempty.

Set $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ with quotient norm $\|[U]\|_{\mathcal D}:=\inf_{w\in H_0^1(\Omega)}\|U+w\|_{H^1(\Omega)}$, and let $\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$ be its continuous conjugate-linear dual. For $f=[U]\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, let $u_{\gamma,f}$ be the unique element of the coset $f$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla z}\,dx=0\qquad(z\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)).$$
Define the weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann map $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$ by
$$\bigl(\Lambda_\gamma f\bigr)(g):=\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla V_g}\,dx,$$
where $V_g$ is any representative of $g\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$. The trace quotient identification makes $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ the $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ boundary data space with its trace quotient norm. Constants lie in the kernel of $\Lambda_\gamma$, and its range functionals annihilate constants; hence $\Lambda_\gamma$ induces $\dot\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1\to(\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1)^*$, the quotient Dirichlet-to-Neumann map used for Calderón stability. Well-posedness, independence from the representative $V_g$, boundedness and the induced quotient map are established by the well-posedness result cited below.

Define $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with its quotient norm. The trace induces a bounded linear bijection $\overline T:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with bounded inverse, so these two norms are equivalent under the induced identification. The induced map after quotienting by constants is also a bounded linear bijection $\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb K\mathbf1\to W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)/\mathbb K$, with equivalent quotient norms. [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and
[[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]]. For an open set
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge1$, an integer $k\ge0$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, set
$$H^k(\Omega;\mathbb K):=W^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$

derivatives and norm are exactly those already defined for $W^{k,2}$. When the

The notation $H^k_0(\Omega)$ is reserved for the later definition by closure of
compactly supported smooth functions in the Sobolev norm. This item assigns no

pointwise vanishing or by traces.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and bounded in one direction: there are a unit vector $e$ and $a<b$ with $a<x\cdot e<b$ for every $x\in\Omega$. Let $1\le p<\infty$. Then $\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C(p)\,(b-a)\,\|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)}$ for every $u\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega;\mathbb K)$.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a real or complex Hilbert space, let $a$ be a bounded coercive sesquilinear form on $H$ with constants $M,\alpha$ ([[def-bounded-coercive-and-symmetric-sesquilinear-forms]]), and let $F:H\to\mathbb K$ be a bounded conjugate-linear functional with norm $\|F\|=\sup_{\|v\|\le1}|F(v)|$. Then there is a unique $u\in H$ with $$a(u,v)=F(v)\qquad\text{for every }v\in H,$$ and it satisfies $\alpha\|u\|\le\|F\|$, that is $\|u\|\le\|F\|/\alpha$. The real bilinear case is the same statement with $a$ symmetric or not, $F$ a bounded linear functional, and the conjugation read as the identity.

derivations.claim:
For $w\in H_0^1(\Omega)$, [F3] gives $\|w\|_{H^1}^2=\|w\|_2^2+\|
abla w\|_2^2\le2\|
abla w\|_2^2$. By [F1], the form $a_\gamma(w,z):=\int_\Omega\gamma
abla w\cdot\overline{
abla z}\,dx$ is bounded by $M\|w\|_{H^1}\|z\|_{H^1}$ and satisfies $a_\gamma(w,w)\ge(m/2)\|w\|_{H^1}^2$. Thus it is bounded and coercive on $H_0^1(\Omega)$.

Choose any representative $U\in f$. The functional $z\mapsto-a_\gamma(U,z)$ is bounded and conjugate-linear on $H_0^1$, with norm at most $M\|U\|_{H^1}$. Lax–Milgram [F4] applied to step 1.1 gives a unique $w\in H_0^1$ satisfying $a_\gamma(w,z)=-a_\gamma(U,z)$ for every $z\in H_0^1$. Then $u:=U+w\in f$ satisfies the required weak equation.

If $u_1,u_2\in f$ both solve the weak equation, then $v:=u_1-u_2\in H_0^1$ by the quotient definition in [F2], and $a_\gamma(v,z)=0$ for every $z\in H_0^1$. Taking $z=v$ gives $m\|\nabla v\|_2^2\le a_\gamma(v,v)=0$; [F3] then gives $\|v\|_2=0$, so $v=0$. This proves uniqueness.

For $f_1,f_2\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ and $c_1,c_2\in\mathbb C$, the function $c_1u_{\gamma,f_1}+c_2u_{\gamma,f_2}$ belongs to the trace class $c_1f_1+c_2f_2$. The weak equation is linear in its solution because the energy form is linear in its first argument, so this combination solves the weak problem for that class. Uniqueness from step 1.3 gives $u_{\gamma,c_1f_1+c_2f_2}=c_1u_{\gamma,f_1}+c_2u_{\gamma,f_2}$. The energy definition is also linear in this first argument, hence $\Lambda_\gamma$ is linear.

If $V_g,V'_g\in g$, then $V_g-V'_g\in H_0^1$ by [F2], so the weak equation for $u_{\gamma,f}$ makes $a_\gamma(u_{\gamma,f},V_g)=a_\gamma(u_{\gamma,f},V'_g)$. Thus the defining functional is independent of the representative.

For a representative $U\in f$, the solution estimate in [F4] and step 1.1 give $\|u_{\gamma,f}\|_{H^1}\le(1+2M/m)\|U\|_{H^1}$. Taking the infimum over representatives gives $\|u_{\gamma,f}\|_{H^1}\le(1+2M/m)\|f\|_{\mathcal D}$. Applying the same representative bound to $g$ yields
$$|a_\gamma(u_{\gamma,f},V_g)|\le M(1+2M/m)^2\|f\|_{\mathcal D}\|g\|_{\mathcal D},$$
so $\Lambda_\gamma$ is bounded into $\mathcal D^*$.

For a constant input $c$, the constant function $u=c$ solves the weak equation and uniqueness gives $u_{\gamma,c}=c$, whose gradient is zero. For a constant test class $c$, its constant representative has zero gradient. The energy formula therefore vanishes on constant inputs and constant tests, so it induces the stated map on the quotient by constants.

$$X_d(R):=\begin{cases}\{\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')\cap BV(\Omega):\|\gamma\|_{BV(\Omega)}\le R\},&d=2,\\[2mm]\{\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')\cap C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega):\|\gamma\|_{C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le R\},&d\ge3.\end{cases}$$
For $\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')$, define its measurable background extension $\gamma_e:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ by $\gamma_e=\gamma$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$ and $\gamma_e=1$ on $\mathbb R^d\setminus\Omega$. Then $\gamma_e-1$ vanishes almost everywhere outside $\Omega'$. No pointwise continuity of $\gamma_e$ is asserted. The classes $X_d(R)$ are not assumed nonempty.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected smooth domain, and let $\gamma\in\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega)$ be a real almost-everywhere class with $0<m\le\gamma\le M<\infty$. Set $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ with quotient norm $\|[U]\|_{\mathcal D}:=\inf_{w\in H_0^1(\Omega)}\|U+w\|_{H^1(\Omega)}$, and let $\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$ be its continuous conjugate-linear dual. For $f=[U]\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, let $u_{\gamma,f}$ be the unique element of the coset $f$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla z}\,dx=0\qquad(z\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)).$$
Define the weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann map $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$ by
$$\bigl(\Lambda_\gamma f\bigr)(g):=\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla V_g}\,dx,$$
where $V_g$ is any representative of $g\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$. The trace quotient identification makes $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ the $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ boundary data space with its trace quotient norm. Constants lie in the kernel of $\Lambda_\gamma$, and its range functionals annihilate constants; hence $\Lambda_\gamma$ induces $\dot\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1\to(\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1)^*$, the quotient Dirichlet-to-Neumann map used for Calderón stability. Well-posedness, independence from the representative $V_g$, boundedness and the induced quotient map are established by the well-posedness result cited below.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $n\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty bounded connected open set whose boundary is covered by finitely many $C^1$ graph charts. Give $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ its Sobolev norm, let $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ be the $H^1$-closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and let $W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ have the finite-chart Slobodeckij norm. Define $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with its quotient norm. The trace induces a bounded linear bijection $\overline T:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with bounded inverse, so these two norms are equivalent under the induced identification. The induced map after quotienting by constants is also a bounded linear bijection $\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb K\mathbf1\to W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)/\mathbb K$, with equivalent quotient norms. A continuous linear functional on $W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ descends to the constant quotient exactly when it annihilates constants, and its descended functional has the quotient dual norm.

Assume Countable Choice, as in
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and
[[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]]. For an open set
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge1$, an integer $k\ge0$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, set
$$H^k(\Omega;\mathbb K):=W^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The elements are the same almost-everywhere classes, and their weak
derivatives and norm are exactly those already defined for $W^{k,2}$. When the
scalar field is fixed, write $H^k(\Omega)$.

The notation $H^k_0(\Omega)$ is reserved for the later definition by closure of
compactly supported smooth functions in the Sobolev norm. This item assigns no
boundary values to an equivalence class and asserts no characterization by
pointwise vanishing or by traces.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and bounded in one direction: there are a unit vector $e$ and $a<b$ with $a<x\cdot e<b$ for every $x\in\Omega$. Let $1\le p<\infty$. Then $\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C(p)\,(b-a)\,\|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)}$ for every $u\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega;\mathbb K)$.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a real or complex Hilbert space, let $a$ be a bounded coercive sesquilinear form on $H$ with constants $M,\alpha$ ([[def-bounded-coercive-and-symmetric-sesquilinear-forms]]), and let $F:H\to\mathbb K$ be a bounded conjugate-linear functional with norm $\|F\|=\sup_{\|v\|\le1}|F(v)|$. Then there is a unique $u\in H$ with $$a(u,v)=F(v)\qquad\text{for every }v\in H,$$ and it satisfies $\alpha\|u\|\le\|F\|$, that is $\|u\|\le\|F\|/\alpha$. The real bilinear case is the same statement with $a$ symmetric or not, $F$ a bounded linear functional, and the conjugation read as the identity.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

For $w\in H_0^1(\Omega)$, [F3] gives $\|w\|_{H^1}^2=\|w\|_2^2+\|
abla w\|_2^2\le2\|

abla w\cdot\overline{
abla z}\,dx$ is bounded by $M\|w\|_{H^1}\|z\|_{H^1}$ and satisfies $a_\gamma(w,w)\ge(m/2)\|w\|_{H^1}^2$. Thus it is bounded and coercive on $H_0^1(\Omega)$.

Choose any representative $U\in f$. The functional $z\mapsto-a_\gamma(U,z)$ is bounded and conjugate-linear on $H_0^1$, with norm at most $M\|U\|_{H^1}$. Lax–Milgram [F4] applied to step 1.1 gives a unique $w\in H_0^1$ satisfying $a_\gamma(w,z)=-a_\gamma(U,z)$ for every $z\in H_0^1$. Then $u:=U+w\in f$ satisfies the required weak equation.

If $u_1,u_2\in f$ both solve the weak equation, then $v:=u_1-u_2\in H_0^1$ by the quotient definition in [F2], and $a_\gamma(v,z)=0$ for every $z\in H_0^1$. Taking $z=v$ gives $m\|\nabla v\|_2^2\le a_\gamma(v,v)=0$; [F3] then gives $\|v\|_2=0$, so $v=0$. This proves uniqueness.

For $f_1,f_2\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ and $c_1,c_2\in\mathbb C$, the function $c_1u_{\gamma,f_1}+c_2u_{\gamma,f_2}$ belongs to the trace class $c_1f_1+c_2f_2$. The weak equation is linear in its solution because the energy form is linear in its first argument, so this combination solves the weak problem for that class. Uniqueness from step 3.1 gives $u_{\gamma,c_1f_1+c_2f_2}=c_1u_{\gamma,f_1}+c_2u_{\gamma,f_2}$. The energy definition is also linear in this first argument, hence $\Lambda_\gamma$ is linear.

If $V_g,V'_g\in g$, then $V_g-V'_g\in H_0^1$ by [F2], so the weak equation for $u_{\gamma,f}$ makes $a_\gamma(u_{\gamma,f},V_g)=a_\gamma(u_{\gamma,f},V'_g)$. Thus the defining functional is independent of the representative.

For a representative $U\in f$, the solution estimate in [F4] and step 1.1 give $\|u_{\gamma,f}\|_{H^1}\le(1+2M/m)\|U\|_{H^1}$. Taking the infimum over representatives gives $\|u_{\gamma,f}\|_{H^1}\le(1+2M/m)\|f\|_{\mathcal D}$. For a constant input $c$, the constant function $u=c$ solves the weak equation and uniqueness gives $u_{\gamma,c}=c$, whose gradient is zero. For a constant test class $c$, its constant representative has zero gradient. The energy formula therefore vanishes on constant inputs and constant tests, so it induces the stated map on the quotient by constants.

> (Choice function).

$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a nonempty compact connected smooth Riemannian domain with nonempty smooth boundary. For a real-valued $\gamma\in C^\infty(M)$ with $\gamma(x)>0$ at every $x\in M$, let $v_f\in H^1(M)$ be the unique weak solution of $\operatorname{div}_g(\gamma\nabla_gv_f)=0$ with trace $f\in H^{1/2}(\partial M)$, whose existence is supplied by the positive-conductivity solvability lemma. Define the full-data physical conductivity Dirichlet-to-Neumann map $\Lambda_\gamma:H^{1/2}(\partial M)\to H^{-1/2}(\partial M)$ by
$$\langle\Lambda_\gamma f,h\rangle=\int_M\gamma\,g(\nabla_gv_f,\nabla_g\overline{V_h})\,dV_g,$$
where $V_h\in H^1(M)$ is any extension of $h\in H^{1/2}(\partial M)$. The weak equation makes this value independent of the extension. For smooth data, $\Lambda_\gamma f=\gamma\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}v_f|_{\partial M}$; this is the full physical flux convention. When $M=\overline\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ with the Euclidean metric, this is the scalar Euclidean conductivity DN map.

For a real $q\in C^\infty(M)$ such that the only $w\in H_0^1(M)$ satisfying $(-\Delta_g+q)w=0$ weakly is $w=0$, let $u_f\in H^1(M)$ be the unique weak solution of $(-\Delta_g+q)u_f=0$ with trace $f$, whose existence follows from the nonresonant regularity lemma. Define the Schrödinger DN map $\Lambda_q:H^{1/2}(\partial M)\to H^{-1/2}(\partial M)$ by
$$\langle\Lambda_qf,h\rangle=\int_M\big(g(\nabla_gu_f,\nabla_g\overline{V_h})+qu_f\overline{V_h}\big)\,dV_g.$$
For smooth data this is $\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}u_f|_{\partial M}$. Equality of these operators means equality on all of $H^{1/2}(\partial M)$, not equality for a restricted set of boundary inputs.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact connected smooth Riemannian domain with nonempty smooth boundary and no orientability assumption, and let $\gamma\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ satisfy $\gamma>0$. There is a constant $C_P>0$ such that $\|w\|_{L^2(M)}\leq C_P\|
abla_gw\|_{L^2(M)}$ for every $w\in H_0^1(M)$. For every $h\in L^2(M)$ and $f\in H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ there is a unique $v\in H^1(M)$ with trace $f$ satisfying $\int_M\gamma\,g(
abla_gv,
abla_g\overline z)\,dV_g=-\int_Mh\overline z\,dV_g$ for every $z\in H_0^1(M)$. If $h$ and $f$ are smooth, this weak solution is smooth up to the boundary.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian domain with smooth boundary and no orientability assumption, let $q\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$, and suppose the only $w\in H_0^1(M)$ satisfying $(-\Delta_g+q)w=0$ weakly is $w=0$. For every $F\in L^2(M)$ and $f\in H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ there is a unique weak solution $u\in H^1(M)$ of $(-\Delta_g+q)u=F$ with trace $f$. If $f=0$, $F\in H^m(M)$ and $m\geq0$ is an integer, then $u\in H^{m+2}(M)$ and $\|u\|_{H^{m+2}}\leq C_m\|F\|_{H^m}$. If $F$ and $f$ are smooth, this solution belongs to $H^m(M)$ for every integer $m\geq0$.

Assume Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary, with no orientability assumption. Fix a finite smooth atlas of interior and boundary charts and a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it. For an integer $k\geq0$, define $H^k(M)$ as the completion of $C^\infty(M)$ in the sum of the Euclidean $W^{k,2}$ norms of the localized coordinate representatives; derivatives in a boundary chart are taken on the corresponding half-space. Define $H_0^1(M)$ as the closure of $C_c^\infty(M^\circ)$ in $H^1(M)$. Define $H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ by the fixed finite boundary atlas and partition of unity, using the Euclidean fractional Slobodeckij space $W^{1/2,2}(\mathbb R^{n-1})$ for each localized representative. Define $H^{-1/2}(\partial M)$ as the continuous dual of $H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ with the Riemannian boundary density pairing. These are the fixed-atlas norms used on this page; no atlas-independence assertion is part of this definition.

For a smooth real function $f$, its **Riemannian gradient** is $\operatorname{grad}_g f=(df)^\sharp$.

[[prop-exterior-derivative-of-a-function-is-its-differential]] identifies $df(X)=Xf$. The smooth bundle isomorphism in [[thm-the-musical-maps-are-smooth-inverse-bundle-isomorphisms]] therefore makes the gradient a smooth vector field. In coordinates $(\operatorname{grad}_g f)^i=\sum_jg^{ij}\partial_jf$. Constants, and all functions in dimension zero, have zero gradient.

Let $(M,g)$ be a Riemannian manifold, possibly with boundary, and let
$f:M\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. At each interior point, the
**Laplace–Beltrami operator** of $g$ is defined by the metric trace of the Hessian,
$$\Delta_gf(p):=\operatorname{tr}_g(\operatorname{Hess}f)_p:=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{Hess}f(e_i,e_i),$$
where $n=\dim M$ and $e_1,\dots,e_n$ is any $g_p$-orthonormal basis of $T_pM$; the
trace of a bilinear form with respect to a positive-definite inner product does not
depend on that choice, so $\Delta_gf$ is well-defined and smooth in the interior;
when $f$ is smooth up to the boundary, it has the usual one-sided extension there.
Here
$\operatorname{Hess}f(X,Y)=g(\nabla_X\operatorname{grad}f,Y)$ is the Levi-Civita
Hessian of
[[prop-gradient-hessian-and-divergence-connection-formulas]].

Equivalently, and with the **positive-divergence convention** of this library,
$$\Delta_gf=\operatorname{div}_g(\operatorname{grad}f),$$
where $\operatorname{div}_gX=\operatorname{tr}(v\mapsto\nabla_vX)$ is the Riemannian
divergence of [[def-riemannian-divergence]] as computed in
[[prop-gradient-hessian-and-divergence-connection-formulas]]. The equivalence is the
pointwise computation
$$\sum_i\operatorname{Hess}f(e_i,e_i)=\sum_i g(\nabla_{e_i}\operatorname{grad}f,e_i)=\operatorname{tr}(v\mapsto\nabla_v\operatorname{grad}f),$$
the middle sum being the endomorphism trace of $v\mapsto\nabla_v\operatorname{grad}f$
in the orthonormal basis $(e_i)$, which the same supplier identifies with
$\operatorname{div}_g(\operatorname{grad}f)$; no local coordinates are needed and no
analytic regularity beyond the smoothness of $f$ is used. On a zero-dimensional manifold
both sides are the empty sum $0$, and on a manifold with boundary the operator is defined
at interior points, with the usual one-sided extension at boundary points when $f$ is
smooth up to the boundary.

**This definition is the pointwise geometric operator only.** It records the trace
formula, the divergence form and the sign convention
$\Delta_g=\operatorname{div}_g\circ\operatorname{grad}$ fixed by
[[def-riemannian-divergence]]. It does not assert any analytic conclusion about
harmonic functions on manifolds — no maximum principle, no Harnack inequality, no
boundary-value solvability, no spectral theory, and no Liouville theorem. Those are
separate results with their own hypotheses, and their Euclidean forms are not licensed
on a general Riemannian manifold merely by writing down this definition.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a nonempty compact connected smooth Riemannian domain with nonempty smooth boundary. For a real-valued $\gamma\in C^\infty(M)$ with $\gamma(x)>0$ at every $x\in M$, let $v_f\in H^1(M)$ be the unique weak solution of $\operatorname{div}_g(\gamma\nabla_gv_f)=0$ with trace $f\in H^{1/2}(\partial M)$, whose existence is supplied by the positive-conductivity solvability lemma. Define the full-data physical conductivity Dirichlet-to-Neumann map $\Lambda_\gamma:H^{1/2}(\partial M)\to H^{-1/2}(\partial M)$ by
$$\langle\Lambda_\gamma f,h\rangle=\int_M\gamma\,g(\nabla_gv_f,\nabla_g\overline{V_h})\,dV_g,$$
where $V_h\in H^1(M)$ is any extension of $h\in H^{1/2}(\partial M)$. The weak equation makes this value independent of the extension. For smooth data, $\Lambda_\gamma f=\gamma\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}v_f|_{\partial M}$; this is the full physical flux convention. When $M=\overline\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ with the Euclidean metric, this is the scalar Euclidean conductivity DN map.

For a real $q\in C^\infty(M)$ such that the only $w\in H_0^1(M)$ satisfying $(-\Delta_g+q)w=0$ weakly is $w=0$, let $u_f\in H^1(M)$ be the unique weak solution of $(-\Delta_g+q)u_f=0$ with trace $f$, whose existence follows from the nonresonant regularity lemma. Define the Schrödinger DN map $\Lambda_q:H^{1/2}(\partial M)\to H^{-1/2}(\partial M)$ by
$$\langle\Lambda_qf,h\rangle=\int_M\big(g(\nabla_gu_f,\nabla_g\overline{V_h})+qu_f\overline{V_h}\big)\,dV_g.$$
For smooth data this is $\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}u_f|_{\partial M}$. Equality of these operators means equality on all of $H^{1/2}(\partial M)$, not equality for a restricted set of boundary inputs.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact connected smooth Riemannian domain with nonempty smooth boundary and no orientability assumption, and let $\gamma\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ satisfy $\gamma>0$. There is a constant $C_P>0$ such that $\|w\|_{L^2(M)}\leq C_P\|
abla_gw\|_{L^2(M)}$ for every $w\in H_0^1(M)$. For every $h\in L^2(M)$ and $f\in H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ there is a unique $v\in H^1(M)$ with trace $f$ satisfying $\int_M\gamma\,g(
abla_gv,
abla_g\overline z)\,dV_g=-\int_Mh\overline z\,dV_g$ for every $z\in H_0^1(M)$. If $h$ and $f$ are smooth, this weak solution is smooth up to the boundary.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian domain with smooth boundary and no orientability assumption, let $q\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$, and suppose the only $w\in H_0^1(M)$ satisfying $(-\Delta_g+q)w=0$ weakly is $w=0$. For every $F\in L^2(M)$ and $f\in H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ there is a unique weak solution $u\in H^1(M)$ of $(-\Delta_g+q)u=F$ with trace $f$. If $f=0$, $F\in H^m(M)$ and $m\geq0$ is an integer, then $u\in H^{m+2}(M)$ and $\|u\|_{H^{m+2}}\leq C_m\|F\|_{H^m}$. If $F$ and $f$ are smooth, this solution belongs to $H^m(M)$ for every integer $m\geq0$.

Assume Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary, with no orientability assumption. Fix a finite smooth atlas of interior and boundary charts and a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it. For an integer $k\geq0$, define $H^k(M)$ as the completion of $C^\infty(M)$ in the sum of the Euclidean $W^{k,2}$ norms of the localized coordinate representatives; derivatives in a boundary chart are taken on the corresponding half-space. Define $H_0^1(M)$ as the closure of $C_c^\infty(M^\circ)$ in $H^1(M)$. Define $H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ by the fixed finite boundary atlas and partition of unity, using the Euclidean fractional Slobodeckij space $W^{1/2,2}(\mathbb R^{n-1})$ for each localized representative. Define $H^{-1/2}(\partial M)$ as the continuous dual of $H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ with the Riemannian boundary density pairing. These are the fixed-atlas norms used on this page; no atlas-independence assertion is part of this definition.

For a smooth real function $f$, its **Riemannian gradient** is $\operatorname{grad}_g f=(df)^\sharp$.

[[prop-exterior-derivative-of-a-function-is-its-differential]] identifies $df(X)=Xf$. The smooth bundle isomorphism in [[thm-the-musical-maps-are-smooth-inverse-bundle-isomorphisms]] therefore makes the gradient a smooth vector field. In coordinates $(\operatorname{grad}_g f)^i=\sum_jg^{ij}\partial_jf$. Constants, and all functions in dimension zero, have zero gradient.

Let $(M,g)$ be a Riemannian manifold, possibly with boundary, and let
$f:M\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. At each interior point, the
**Laplace–Beltrami operator** of $g$ is defined by the metric trace of the Hessian,
$$\Delta_gf(p):=\operatorname{tr}_g(\operatorname{Hess}f)_p:=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{Hess}f(e_i,e_i),$$
where $n=\dim M$ and $e_1,\dots,e_n$ is any $g_p$-orthonormal basis of $T_pM$; the
trace of a bilinear form with respect to a positive-definite inner product does not
depend on that choice, so $\Delta_gf$ is well-defined and smooth in the interior;
when $f$ is smooth up to the boundary, it has the usual one-sided extension there.
Here
$\operatorname{Hess}f(X,Y)=g(\nabla_X\operatorname{grad}f,Y)$ is the Levi-Civita
Hessian of
[[prop-gradient-hessian-and-divergence-connection-formulas]].

Equivalently, and with the **positive-divergence convention** of this library,
$$\Delta_gf=\operatorname{div}_g(\operatorname{grad}f),$$
where $\operatorname{div}_gX=\operatorname{tr}(v\mapsto\nabla_vX)$ is the Riemannian
divergence of [[def-riemannian-divergence]] as computed in
[[prop-gradient-hessian-and-divergence-connection-formulas]]. The equivalence is the
pointwise computation
$$\sum_i\operatorname{Hess}f(e_i,e_i)=\sum_i g(\nabla_{e_i}\operatorname{grad}f,e_i)=\operatorname{tr}(v\mapsto\nabla_v\operatorname{grad}f),$$
the middle sum being the endomorphism trace of $v\mapsto\nabla_v\operatorname{grad}f$
in the orthonormal basis $(e_i)$, which the same supplier identifies with
$\operatorname{div}_g(\operatorname{grad}f)$; no local coordinates are needed and no
analytic regularity beyond the smoothness of $f$ is used. On a zero-dimensional manifold
both sides are the empty sum $0$, and on a manifold with boundary the operator is defined
at interior points, with the usual one-sided extension at boundary points when $f$ is
smooth up to the boundary.

**This definition is the pointwise geometric operator only.** It records the trace
formula, the divergence form and the sign convention
$\Delta_g=\operatorname{div}_g\circ\operatorname{grad}$ fixed by
[[def-riemannian-divergence]]. It does not assert any analytic conclusion about
harmonic functions on manifolds — no maximum principle, no Harnack inequality, no
boundary-value solvability, no spectral theory, and no Liouville theorem. Those are
separate results with their own hypotheses, and their Euclidean forms are not licensed
on a general Riemannian manifold merely by writing down this definition.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary, with no orientability assumption. Fix a finite smooth atlas of interior and boundary charts and a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it. For an integer $k\geq0$, define $H^k(M)$ as the completion of $C^\infty(M)$ in the sum of the Euclidean $W^{k,2}$ norms of the localized coordinate representatives; derivatives in a boundary chart are taken on the corresponding half-space. Define $H_0^1(M)$ as the closure of $C_c^\infty(M^\circ)$ in $H^1(M)$. Define $H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ by the fixed finite boundary atlas and partition of unity, using the Euclidean fractional Slobodeckij space $W^{1/2,2}(\mathbb R^{n-1})$ for each localized representative. Define $H^{-1/2}(\partial M)$ as the continuous dual of $H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ with the Riemannian boundary density pairing. These are the fixed-atlas norms used on this page; no atlas-independence assertion is part of this definition.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a
bounded open set and let $1\le p<\infty$. Then $W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)$ is
compactly embedded in $L^p(\Omega)$: the inclusion is bounded, and every
sequence bounded in $W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)$ has a subsequence converging in
$L^p(\Omega)$. No regularity of $\partial\Omega$ is needed.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a real or complex Hilbert space, let $a$ be a bounded coercive sesquilinear form on $H$ with constants $M,\alpha$ ([[def-bounded-coercive-and-symmetric-sesquilinear-forms]]), and let $F:H\to\mathbb K$ be a bounded conjugate-linear functional with norm $\|F\|=\sup_{\|v\|\le1}|F(v)|$. Then there is a unique $u\in H$ with $$a(u,v)=F(v)\qquad\text{for every }v\in H,$$ and it satisfies $\alpha\|u\|\le\|F\|$, that is $\|u\|\le\|F\|/\alpha$. The real bilinear case is the same statement with $a$ symmetric or not, $F$ a bounded linear functional, and the conjugation read as the identity.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a
bounded $C^1$ domain in the graph sense of
[[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]], let $\partial\Omega$ carry the
chart-independent surface measure of
[[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]] and
[[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]], let
$1\le p<\infty$ and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Then there is a
unique bounded linear operator
$$T:W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)\longrightarrow L^p(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$$
with $Tu=u|_{\partial\Omega}$ for every
$u\in C(\overline\Omega)\cap W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and it satisfies
$\|Tu\|_{L^p(\partial\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,p)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}$. On each
boundary chart the operator is the flat half-space trace of
[[thm-trace-estimate-on-the-half-space]] transported by the flattening
diffeomorphism, and the chartwise definitions agree on overlaps; uniqueness
holds because two bounded operators agreeing on the dense subspace
$C(\overline\Omega)\cap W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ are equal.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a
bounded $C^1$ domain, $1<p<\infty$, $\theta=1-1/p$, and let $T$ be the trace
operator of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]. Then there is
a bounded linear operator
$$R:W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)\longrightarrow W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$$
with $T\circ R=\mathrm{id}_{W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)}$ and
$\|Rg\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,p)\|g\|_{W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)}$.
Moreover, for every open neighbourhood $U$ of $\partial\Omega$ in
$\mathbb R^n$ there is such an operator $R_U$ whose image is contained in the
classes vanishing a.e. outside $U$, with
$\|R_Ug\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,p,U)\|g\|_{W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)}$.
The right inverse is not unique and no canonical choice is claimed.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded
$C^{k+2}$ domain, $n\ge2$, $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let
$k\ge0$, let $L,a$ be as in
[[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]] with
$a^{ij}\in W^{k+1,\infty}(\Omega)$, $b^i,c\in W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ and all
coefficient derivatives bounded, and let $f\in H^k(\Omega)$. If
$u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ is a weak solution of $Lu=f$ with zero boundary values
([[def-weak-dirichlet-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]), then
$u\in H^{k+2}(\Omega)$ and
$$\|u\|_{H^{k+2}(\Omega)}\le C\big(\|f\|_{H^k(\Omega)}+\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\big),$$
with $C$ depending only on $n,k,\Omega$ and the coefficient bounds. The
derivative gain is exactly two orders; the boundary regularity required at
order $k$ is $C^{k+2}$, the coefficient regularity one order above the data
order, and the companion page records the sharp two-derivative example. For
$k=0$ the theorem is
[[thm-global-h-two-dirichlet-regularity]].

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega$ be a bounded $W^{k,p}$-extension domain, $k\ge1$ and $1\le p<\infty$. Let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and $u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Then:

1. if $kp<n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every $q$ with $\frac1q\ge\frac1p-\frac kn$ (equivalently $1\le q\le\frac{np}{n-kp}$);
2. if $kp=n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C(q)\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every finite $q$;
3. if $kp>n$, then for every integer $m\ge0$ and every $0<\alpha<1$ with $m+\alpha<k-\frac np$ there is a representative in $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ with $\|u\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$; when $k-\frac np\notin\mathbb Z$ one may take $m=\lfloor k-\frac np\rfloor$ and $\alpha=k-\frac np-m$.

Here $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ uses the continuous derivatives of the constructed representative on an ambient neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$, with norm
$$\|g\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\sum_{|\beta|\le m}\sup_{\overline\Omega}|D^\beta g|+\sum_{|\beta|=m}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|D^\beta g(x)-D^\beta g(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}.$$
For $\Omega=\varnothing$ set these norm values to $0$. The proof supplies such an ambient representative, so no boundary differentiability or regularity of $\partial\Omega$ is assumed.
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every smooth manifold with boundary has a smooth collar.

derivations.claim: There is a constant $C_P$ such that $\|w\|_{L^2(M)}\leq C_P\|\nabla w\|_{L^2(M)}$ for $w\in H_0^1(M)$. Otherwise choose $w_j\in H_0^1(M)$ with $\|w_j\|_{L^2}=1$ and $\|\nabla w_j\|_{L^2}\to0$. The sequence is bounded in $H^1$. A finite chart partition and [F2] give an $L^2$-convergent subsequence; a further subsequence converges weakly in the Hilbert space $H^1$, so its limit $w$ belongs to the weakly closed subspace $H_0^1(M)$, has weak gradient zero, and has $L^2$ norm one. In each connected coordinate ball, convolution of a function with zero weak gradient is constant on smaller balls; overlapping balls force the constants to agree, so connectedness makes $w$ constant on $M^\circ$. Its trace is zero by [F4], whereas the trace of a nonzero constant is that same nonzero constant on the nonempty boundary. This contradiction proves the inequality.

Compactness of $M$ and positivity of $\gamma$ give $\gamma_*:=\min_M\gamma>0$. Thus $a_\gamma(w,z)=\int_M\gamma\,g(\nabla w,\nabla\bar z)\,dV_g$ is bounded on $H_0^1(M)$ and $a_\gamma(w,w)\geq c\|w\|_{H^1(M)}^2$ by step 1.1 and $\gamma_*$. By [F3], for any bounded conjugate-linear functional $G$ on $H_0^1(M)$ there is a unique $w\in H_0^1(M)$ with $a_\gamma(w,z)=G(z)$ for all $z$.

Flatten each boundary chart, apply the local half-space trace lift, and patch the finitely many chart lifts with a smooth partition. The resulting $Ef\in H^1(M)$ has trace $f$ and norm bounded by $C\|f\|_{H^{1/2}(\partial M)}$ by [F5]. For $h\in L^2(M)$ take $G(z)=-\int_Mh\overline z\,dV_g-a_\gamma(Ef,z)$ in step 2.1 and set $v=Ef+w$. Then $v$ has trace $f$ and satisfies the weak equation. If $v_1,v_2$ are two such solutions, their difference $w$ lies in $H_0^1$ and $a_\gamma(w,w)=0$; since $\gamma\geq\gamma_*>0$, $\nabla w=0$, and step 1.1 gives $w=0$.

Suppose $h$ and $f$ are smooth. By [F8], extend $f$ smoothly from the boundary into a collar and multiply by a cutoff to obtain a smooth extension $Ef$ on $M$. Then $w=v-Ef$ has zero trace and solves $\operatorname{div}_g(\gamma\nabla_gw)=h-\operatorname{div}_g(\gamma\nabla_gEf)$, whose right-hand side is smooth. In each boundary chart, flatten the boundary and write the principal matrix as $|g|^{1/2}\gamma g^{ij}$; it is smooth and uniformly elliptic because $g$ is positive definite and $\gamma$ has a positive minimum. For the base case, localize $w$ by a cutoff; its equation has an $L^2$ right-hand side since $w\in H^1$, so [F6] gives local $H^2$ regularity. If $w\in H^{m+1}$, each cutoff commutator contains derivatives of $w$ of order at most $m+1$ with smooth bounded coefficients, hence lies in $H^m$; the localized right-hand side is therefore in $H^m$, and [F6] gives $H^{m+2}$ regularity. Induction over $m$ and a finite chart cover give $w\in H^m(M)$ for every integer $m$. By [F7], $w$ and hence $v=Ef+w$ are smooth up to the boundary.
