derivations.claim: First consider smooth concordances. Pick one point on each endpoint knot. By [F4], apply separate endpoint ambient isotopies carrying both marked points to a common point $p\in S^3$; extend them over disjoint product collars of the concordance and interpolate by the identity between the collars. This changes the representatives only within their ambient-isotopy classes. Choose a smooth spanning arc in each annulus joining the marked points and fixed in product collars. For one annulus, write this arc as $\alpha$ and the standard product arc as $\beta(s)=(p,s)$. Since $S^3\times(0,1)$ is simply connected by [F3], the middle portions of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are homotopic rel endpoints after their common endpoint collars are deleted. Relative smooth approximation in [F3] gives a smooth homotopy $H(s,t)$ fixed on those collars. We now perturb this homotopy through a finite-dimensional family. First, local coordinate bumps whose $s$-derivatives span the four target coordinates at each zero of $\partial_sH$ make the total derivative family transverse to the zero section of the rank-four tangent bundle; its source has dimension two, so a generic parameter has $\partial_sH\ne0$ everywhere. Compactness then supplies a uniform $\delta>0$ for local injectivity of every slice when $|s-s'|<\delta$. On the compact configuration set $|s-s'|\ge\delta$, use two disjoint source-supported coordinate bumps near each pair to vary $H(s,t)$ and $H(s',t)$ independently. A finite cover of the possible diagonal preimage makes the total pair map transverse to the diagonal in $(S^3\times I)^2$. Its source-pair-time dimension is three and the diagonal has codimension four, so the generic slice has no double points. Both perturbations are supported away from the endpoint collars and can be chosen small enough to preserve immersion and local injectivity. Thus every time-slice is a smooth embedding, giving an isotopy of proper arcs rel collars. The isotopy is stationary on common source end collars, so restrict to the compact middle arcs containing its moving part; these lie in $S^3\times(0,1)$, a boundaryless smooth manifold. Apply [F3] there with support in the interior, choosing the extension to fix the adjacent stationary arc collars, and extend it by the identity across the fixed end collars. This gives an ambient isotopy of $S^3\times I$ fixed near both end levels and carrying the whole spanning arc to the vertical product arc without changing the concordance or its oriented endpoint knot types.

For each vertical arc, double the ambient product across its two boundary levels by gluing to a second copy of $S^3\times I$, and glue a second copy of the concordance annulus using its product collars. The doubled ambient manifold is $S^3\times S^1$ and the doubled annulus is a smooth embedded torus. Doubling the spanning arc across its endpoints gives a smooth embedded circle $C$ in that torus. Apply the tubular-neighborhood theorem to the closed torus in $S^3\times S^1$ and to $C$ inside the torus. Over $C$, the normal line of $C$ in the torus and the rank-two normal bundle of the torus in the ambient manifold are trivial, so their product gives a neighborhood $D^1\times D^2\times S^1$ of $C$ whose intersection with the torus is exactly $D^1\times S^1$. Restrict to the half corresponding to the original arc; this gives the required product neighborhood $D^3\times I$ meeting the original annulus exactly in $D^1\times I$, with product end faces from the collars. Removing the interior of this strip from each annulus leaves a rectangle. Remove the two product neighborhoods from two copies of $S^3\times I$ and glue their boundary cylinders $S^2\times I$ by the fixed product identification. At each level this glues two three-balls along their boundary spheres, giving $S^3\#S^3\cong S^3$; since the gluing is independent of the interval parameter, the resulting ambient cobordism is $S^3\times I$. Glue the two surface rectangles across the two side intervals in the connecting cylinder, choosing the side identifications to extend the orientations on the cut annuli. At the lower end the fixed orientation-reversing boundary map joins the incoming arcs with boundary orientation $-(K_0\#J_0)$; at the upper end the same product convention gives $K_1\#J_1$. The result is connected, orientable, has two boundary circles, and has Euler characteristic $0$ (two rectangles, each of Euler characteristic $1$, glued along two intervals); hence it is an annulus. The product collars give the required smooth concordance.
The preceding construction proves the smooth implication.

For the TOP implication, first code the actual input as compact metric data. Parametrize the two annuli by the standard compact annulus, and choose finitely many local pair charts covering each, together with their inverses and the given end-collar maps. Such a finite selection is possible by compactness and finite choice; using countably many relatively compact chart restrictions instead would require only $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Include the endpoint knots and the chosen connected-sum representatives from [F2]. For these smooth knots and the finite smooth coordinate maps used in their sums, also code the derivatives of every finite order, their continuity moduli and rational difference-quotient remainder bounds; thus the inner model sees smooth knots, not merely continuous embeddings. Continuous maps on these standard metric domains are coded by their values on fixed countable rational dense sets and uniform continuity moduli on compact exhaustions; include inverse moduli for embeddings and chart inverses. All this countable numerical data is one real $r$.

We use certificates, not an unqualified assertion that homeomorphism existence is absolute. For every open chart domain record its rational-ball code (relative rational half-balls at a boundary chart), compact exhaustion, and positive-distance margins putting the images of exhaustion pieces in the corresponding open image. Record both map/inverse identities on dense sets. For the pair condition record the parametrization of the linear plane section and its identities with the annulus parametrization; on smaller charts also record positive separation from the compact remainder of the annulus outside that patch. A finite parameter-patch cover and a Lebesgue-number certificate cover the entire annulus. Properness is certified on the compact subannuli $S^1\times[1/j,1-1/j]$ by positive separation from the ambient end levels. Equalities with the oriented endpoint parametrizations and the product collars are dense-set equalities with their continuity moduli. The smooth derivative identities are certified by rational difference quotients and their coded remainder bounds at each finite order. These certificates express input validity using only rational inequalities, integer indices and quantification over natural numbers. They therefore have the same truth in $L[r]$ and in the ambient universe; in particular the coded input is valid in $L[r]$.

Apply [F6] inside $L[r]$, which satisfies full Choice by [F7]. It gives a locally flat annulus for the two connected sums. In that model choose its finite pair-chart cover, inverse maps, compact-exhaustion moduli, open-image margins and end-collar certificates of the same form as in step 2.2; collect them into a real $s\in L[r]$. Decode $s$ in the ambient universe by completion from the rational dense domains. The coded forward and inverse moduli give continuous inverse maps on their coded domains; the dense-set identities extend to all points, and the open-image and separation certificates make these actual local pair charts with no additional surface branch. The finite cover certificate, properness margins, and endpoint/collar identities likewise persist. Thus the decoded object is an actual oriented proper locally flat annulus in the ambient $S^3\times I$, with the required endpoint connected sums and product collars. This transfer uses arithmetic certificates for the particular compact objects, not preservation of arbitrary sets or homeomorphisms between inner models.

Together with the retained smooth construction in steps 1.1–3.1, this proves both implications in the unchanged Statement. No annulus-adapted transverse tube or ambient complement is inferred from the bare-arc theorem [F5]; that former local proof gap is bypassed by the explicitly external input [F6].

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3$ be the image of a smooth embedding of the standard $S^2$. There is a smooth ambient isotopy $H_t:S^3\to S^3$, with $H_0=\operatorname{id}$, such that $H_1(S)$ is the standard equatorial sphere $E$. In particular $S^3\setminus S$ has exactly two components. Their closures $B_+$ and $B_-$ are smoothly embedded standard closed $3$-balls with common boundary $S$. If $D_+$ and $D_-$ denote the standard closed hemispheres bounded by $E$, the labels can be chosen so that the restrictions $H_1:B_\pm\to D_\pm$ are diffeomorphisms with the same boundary restriction $H_1|_S:S\to E$. Thus the ball identifications are compatible on their boundary and on a common two-sided collar of that boundary.

Assume countable choice, as required for the smooth normal-bundle structure in the tubular-neighbourhood interface. Let $K:S^1\to S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $\nu(K)=TS^3|_K/TK$ be its quotient normal bundle. Equip $\nu(K)$ with a chosen smooth fibre norm $\|\cdot\|$. Let $\Phi:\Omega\to S^3$ be a tubular-neighbourhood map from an open neighbourhood $\Omega$ of the zero section in $\nu(K)$ that restricts to the inclusion of $K$. For $\epsilon>0$, define the closed disk subbundle
$$
D_\epsilon\nu(K):=\{v\in\nu(K):\|v\|\le\epsilon\}.
$$
Choose $\epsilon$ so that $D_\epsilon\nu(K)\subseteq\Omega$, and set $N(K)=\Phi(D_\epsilon\nu(K))$. The fibre norm, tubular map, and radius are part of the chosen tubular data. The **exterior** of this chosen tube is
$$
E_K:=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}_{S^3}N(K).
$$
Retain its boundary $T_K:=\partial E_K=\partial N(K)$, orient $E_K$ by restriction of the fixed orientation of $S^3$, and orient $T_K$ as the boundary of $E_K$. The choice of tubular map and radius is part of the input to this definition.

derivations.claim: By [F2], $S^3\setminus S$ has two components. The connected set $K$ is disjoint from $S$, so it lies in one component. The connected neighborhood $N(K)$ is also disjoint from $S$ and contains $K$, hence it lies in that same component.
The closure of the other component is a smooth three-ball disjoint from $N(K)$, so it is contained in $E_K$ and has boundary $S$. This proves irreducibility of the chosen exterior.

Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism from $(Y_0,K_0)$ to $(Y_1,K_1)$, and fix $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. Choose a parametrized Kirby decomposition of $W$, together with admissible Heegaard data and regular almost-complex structures for its elementary pieces. Intermediate pieces may contain links with several components or more than one pair of basepoints. Use the colored multipointed modules with $g+n-1$ attaching curves in $\operatorname{Sym}^{g+n-1}(S)$, and specialize all $w$-colors to $U$ and all $z$-colors to $V$; the displayed doubly pointed formula is the $n=1$ case. For a piece represented by a subordinate Heegaard triple $(S,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,\boldsymbol\gamma,w,z)$, its triangle-count map has the form
$$
\mathbf x\longmapsto \sum_{\mathbf y}\ \sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma},\mathbf y)\\ \mu(\phi)=0,\ \mathfrak s(\phi)=\mathfrak s}} \#_2\bigl(\mathcal M(\phi)\bigr)U^{n_w(\phi)}V^{n_z(\phi)}\mathbf y,
$$
where $\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma}$ denotes a chosen cycle representative of the distinguished top-degree homology class of the appropriate standard auxiliary Heegaard pair, $\mathfrak s(\phi)$ is the Spin-c structure determined by the triangle class, and the other symbols and coefficient ring are as in the two-color target definition. For a chosen auxiliary cycle with finite support $\Theta=\sum_j p_j\theta_j$, with $p_j\in\mathbb F_2[U,V]$ and basis generators $\theta_j$, interpret the displayed formula by $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-linearity as $\sum_j p_j F(\mathbf x,\theta_j)$ (or $\sum_j p_j F(\theta_j,\mathbf x)$ for the alpha-triple convention). Compose the elementary maps in the chosen decomposition to obtain a representative
$$
\widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s,\mathcal K}: CFL^-_{UV}(Y_0,K_0,\mathfrak s|_{Y_0})\longrightarrow CFL^-_{UV}(Y_1,K_1,\mathfrak s|_{Y_1}).
$$
The subscript $\mathcal K$ records the chosen decomposition and auxiliary data. This is one map for one Spin-c structure; maps for different Spin-c structures are not summed unless a sum is explicitly specified. derivations.claim: Send the w-regions and z-regions of the given surface to the two colors $U,V$. The source ring is now exactly $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$ and its variable-power filtration is exactly the specified two-coordinate filtration. The curvature vanishes by the two-color identity. citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere, with chosen minimum-genus oriented Seifert surfaces. A normalized $CFK^\infty(K)$ is a free finite-rank chain complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with two integer filtrations $(i,j)$, where multiplication by $U$ lowers both coordinates by one. Give the connected sum $K\#J$ the fixed oriented gluing convention and the sum filtrations and Maslov/Alexander gradings. Then $CFK^\infty(K\#J)$ is bifiltered chain homotopy equivalent to $CFK^\infty(K)\otimes_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}CFK^\infty(J)$, with an equivalence and homotopies preserving both filtration coordinates. Moreover, the normalized finite filtered hat complex of $K\#J$ is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to $C_K\otimes C_J$ with tensor filtration $F_s(C_K\otimes C_J)=\sum_{p+q\le s}F_pC_K\otimes F_qC_J$. Consequently,
$$\tau(K\#J)=\tau(K)+\tau(J).$$

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its normalized bifiltered complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$. The complex of the reverse mirror $-K$ is filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to the dual complex $C(K)^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}(C(K),\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}])$, with dual differential $d\phi(x)=\phi(\partial x)$ and dual basis elements at negated bifiltration coordinates. There is also a Maslov-graded filtered-chain-homotopy equivalence from $C(K)$ to the complex obtained by exchanging the algebraic and Alexander filtrations. These are distinct symmetries: duality negates both filtration coordinates, while conjugation exchanges them.

Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Let $F$ be a compact connected oriented Seifert surface with boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal H=(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,w,z)$ be an admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagram representing $(K,F)$. The associated one-pointed hat chain complex $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is the finite-dimensional chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from the minus complex by setting its basepoint variable to zero; its differential counts index-one disks with zero multiplicity at $w$. Assume for this specified data that the differential is nonincreasing in the Alexander filtration, that the absolute Alexander formula below takes integer values, and that $H(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))\cong\mathbb F_2$. Give a generator $\mathbf x$ its absolute Alexander filtration
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field assigned to $\mathbf x$ by the pointed Morse construction, with its prescribed boundary data near the two basepoints; $c_1$ is the first Chern class of the oriented plane field perpendicular to that vector field. To form the zero-framed surgery, remove a tubular neighborhood of $K$ and glue in a solid torus whose meridian is the longitude induced by $F$. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by deleting a boundary collar of $F$ and capping its longitude by the meridian disk of that solid torus. This is the standard integer normalization, with the one-generator diagram of the standard unknot at filtration zero. The subcomplex $F_s\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is spanned by generators of Alexander filtration at most $s$.

More generally, a finite integer-filtered chain complex is a finite-dimensional chain complex $C$ over $\mathbb F_2$ with subcomplexes $F_sC$ such that $F_sC=0$ for all sufficiently small integers $s$ and $F_sC=C$ for all sufficiently large integers $s$. If $H(C)\cong\mathbb F_2$, define
$$\tau(C):=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z:\operatorname{im}(H(F_sC)\longrightarrow H(C))\ne0\}.$$
For the fixed diagram and surface above, write $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)=\tau(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H),F_*\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))$. Once diagram and surface independence is proved, their common value is the knot invariant $\tau(K)$. Until that comparison is proved, $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)$ denotes only the value for the specified data.

Assume countable choice. Let $F\subset B^4\subset\mathbb R^4$ be a compact connected oriented smoothly properly embedded surface of genus $g$, with its supplied smooth boundary collar and oriented boundary the knot $K\subset S^3$. There is an orientation-preserving ambient diffeomorphism $\Psi:B^4\to B^4$ equal to the identity on a neighborhood of the outer boundary, and $0<\varepsilon<1$, such that $\Psi(F)\cap B^4_\varepsilon$ is exactly a flat two-disk in a plane through $0$. The surface $\Psi(F)\setminus\operatorname{int}B^4_\varepsilon$, in the explicitly round shell $B^4\setminus\operatorname{int}B^4_\varepsilon\cong S^3\times[0,1]$, is a connected smooth oriented knot cobordism between $K$ and a standard unknot, with genus $g$ and Euler characteristic $-2g$. Both boundary components have product collars in a shell identification fixing $K$ and the inner sphere. The ambient diffeomorphism $\Psi$ fixes a sufficiently small restriction of the supplied outer collar; the shell coordinates may be adjusted there to make that surface collar a product. No assertion about the complement of an arbitrary embedded four-ball is used.

derivations.claim: Let $C$ be the normalized finite filtered hat complex for a knot and put $t=\tau(C)$. Choose a cycle $x\in F_tC_n$ representing the generator of $H(C)\cong\mathbb F_2$ in degree $n$. By minimality of $t$, every cycle in $F_{t-1}C_n$ is a boundary. Hence $x\notin B_n+F_{t-1}C_n$, where $B_n=\operatorname{im}(\partial_{n+1})$; otherwise $x-b$ would be a cycle in $F_{t-1}C_n$ representing the same nonzero class. Extend a linear functional $\lambda:C_n\to\mathbb F_2$ that vanishes on $B_n+F_{t-1}C_n$ and satisfies $\lambda(x)=1$. It is a cocycle and represents the nonzero class in the dual homology, since it evaluates nontrivially on the cycle $x$. By [F3], the reflected knot's normalized Laurent complex is the R-dual with both coordinates negated. In the normalized $i=0$ hat slice, the $U^0$ terms are exactly the hat differential, while positive $U$ powers leave that slice in both original and dual complexes; transposing therefore gives the finite hat dual. Negating the Alexander coordinate gives its annihilator filtration $F_sC^\vee=\{\mu:\mu(F_{-s-1}C)=0\}$. Thus $\lambda\in F_{-t}C^\vee$, so $\tau(C^\vee)\le -t$. If $s<-t$, then $-s-1\ge t$ and every functional in $F_sC^\vee$ annihilates $F_tC$, hence pairs trivially with $[x]$. The evaluation pairing identifies $H(C^\vee)$ with $H(C)^\vee$ and is nondegenerate; therefore no such lower filtration level maps nontrivially to total dual homology. This gives $\tau(C^\vee)\ge -t$, and hence $\tau(-K)=-\tau(K)$ in the normalized knot setting.

Choose a smooth embedded arc on $S$ joining its two boundary components. Cut $S$ along a thin strip about that arc, and remove from $S^3\times I$ the interior of a compatible tubular neighborhood of the arc. A properly embedded arc joining the two boundary spheres in this simply connected four-dimensional product is isotopic to a product arc relative its ends: a generic homotopy of such arcs is a path of embeddings, since the coincidence condition for two distinct arc points at the same time has dimension $1+1+1-4<0$, and the derivative-zero condition is also avoidable. These are finitely many compact smooth general-position choices. Removing the product arc neighborhood turns the ambient shell into $B^4$, after rounding its product corners. The cut surface has one boundary component $K_1\#(-K_0)$ and Euler characteristic $\chi(S)+1=1-2g$, hence genus $g$. Its product collars supply the ordinary connected-sum boundary convention. Thus it is an actual smooth genus-$g$ spanning surface for $K_1\#(-K_0)$.

By [F2] and the surface from step 1.2,
$$|\tau(K_1\#(-K_0))|\le g_4(K_1\#(-K_0))\le g.$$
Using connected-sum additivity from [F3] and the threshold sign established in step 1.1 gives $\tau(K_1\#(-K_0))=\tau(K_1)-\tau(K_0)$. This proves the stated inequality. If $g=0$, it gives concordance invariance. If one boundary knot is the standard unknot, [F4] gives the four-ball genus estimate; equivalently, puncture an actual spanning surface and use [F5] to obtain that cobordism case. The only external genus assertion used is Hom's direct $\mathbb F_2$ theorem [F2]; no coefficient transfer from the integral surgery-trace maps is made.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere, with chosen minimum-genus oriented Seifert surfaces. A normalized $CFK^\infty(K)$ is a free finite-rank chain complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with two integer filtrations $(i,j)$, where multiplication by $U$ lowers both coordinates by one. Give the connected sum $K\#J$ the fixed oriented gluing convention and the sum filtrations and Maslov/Alexander gradings. Then $CFK^\infty(K\#J)$ is bifiltered chain homotopy equivalent to $CFK^\infty(K)\otimes_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}CFK^\infty(J)$, with an equivalence and homotopies preserving both filtration coordinates. Moreover, the normalized finite filtered hat complex of $K\#J$ is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to $C_K\otimes C_J$ with tensor filtration $F_s(C_K\otimes C_J)=\sum_{p+q\le s}F_pC_K\otimes F_qC_J$. Consequently,
$$\tau(K\#J)=\tau(K)+\tau(J).$$

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its normalized bifiltered complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$. The complex of the reverse mirror $-K$ is filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to the dual complex $C(K)^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}(C(K),\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}])$, with dual differential $d\phi(x)=\phi(\partial x)$ and dual basis elements at negated bifiltration coordinates. There is also a Maslov-graded filtered-chain-homotopy equivalence from $C(K)$ to the complex obtained by exchanging the algebraic and Alexander filtrations. These are distinct symmetries: duality negates both filtration coordinates, while conjugation exchanges them.

Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Let $F$ be a compact connected oriented Seifert surface with boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal H=(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,w,z)$ be an admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagram representing $(K,F)$. The associated one-pointed hat chain complex $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is the finite-dimensional chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from the minus complex by setting its basepoint variable to zero; its differential counts index-one disks with zero multiplicity at $w$. Assume for this specified data that the differential is nonincreasing in the Alexander filtration, that the absolute Alexander formula below takes integer values, and that $H(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))\cong\mathbb F_2$. Give a generator $\mathbf x$ its absolute Alexander filtration
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field assigned to $\mathbf x$ by the pointed Morse construction, with its prescribed boundary data near the two basepoints; $c_1$ is the first Chern class of the oriented plane field perpendicular to that vector field. To form the zero-framed surgery, remove a tubular neighborhood of $K$ and glue in a solid torus whose meridian is the longitude induced by $F$. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by deleting a boundary collar of $F$ and capping its longitude by the meridian disk of that solid torus. This is the standard integer normalization, with the one-generator diagram of the standard unknot at filtration zero. The subcomplex $F_s\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is spanned by generators of Alexander filtration at most $s$.

More generally, a finite integer-filtered chain complex is a finite-dimensional chain complex $C$ over $\mathbb F_2$ with subcomplexes $F_sC$ such that $F_sC=0$ for all sufficiently small integers $s$ and $F_sC=C$ for all sufficiently large integers $s$. If $H(C)\cong\mathbb F_2$, define
$$\tau(C):=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z:\operatorname{im}(H(F_sC)\longrightarrow H(C))\ne0\}.$$
For the fixed diagram and surface above, write $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)=\tau(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H),F_*\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))$. Once diagram and surface independence is proved, their common value is the knot invariant $\tau(K)$. Until that comparison is proved, $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)$ denotes only the value for the specified data.

Assume countable choice. Let $F\subset B^4\subset\mathbb R^4$ be a compact connected oriented smoothly properly embedded surface of genus $g$, with its supplied smooth boundary collar and oriented boundary the knot $K\subset S^3$. There is an orientation-preserving ambient diffeomorphism $\Psi:B^4\to B^4$ equal to the identity on a neighborhood of the outer boundary, and $0<\varepsilon<1$, such that $\Psi(F)\cap B^4_\varepsilon$ is exactly a flat two-disk in a plane through $0$. The surface $\Psi(F)\setminus\operatorname{int}B^4_\varepsilon$, in the explicitly round shell $B^4\setminus\operatorname{int}B^4_\varepsilon\cong S^3\times[0,1]$, is a connected smooth oriented knot cobordism between $K$ and a standard unknot, with genus $g$ and Euler characteristic $-2g$. Both boundary components have product collars in a shell identification fixing $K$ and the inner sphere. The ambient diffeomorphism $\Psi$ fixes a sufficiently small restriction of the supplied outer collar; the shell coordinates may be adjusted there to make that surface collar a product. No assertion about the complement of an arbitrary embedded four-ball is used.

derivations.claim: Let $C$ be the normalized finite filtered hat complex for a knot and put $t=\tau(C)$. Choose a cycle $x\in F_tC_n$ representing the generator of $H(C)\cong\mathbb F_2$ in degree $n$. By minimality of $t$, every cycle in $F_{t-1}C_n$ is a boundary. Hence $x\notin B_n+F_{t-1}C_n$, where $B_n=\operatorname{im}(\partial_{n+1})$; otherwise $x-b$ would be a cycle in $F_{t-1}C_n$ representing the same nonzero class. Extend a linear functional $\lambda:C_n\to\mathbb F_2$ that vanishes on $B_n+F_{t-1}C_n$ and satisfies $\lambda(x)=1$. It is a cocycle and represents the nonzero class in the dual homology, since it evaluates nontrivially on the cycle $x$. By [F3], the reflected knot's normalized Laurent complex is the R-dual with both coordinates negated. In the normalized $i=0$ hat slice, the $U^0$ terms are exactly the hat differential, while positive $U$ powers leave that slice in both original and dual complexes; transposing therefore gives the finite hat dual. Negating the Alexander coordinate gives its annihilator filtration $F_sC^\vee=\{\mu:\mu(F_{-s-1}C)=0\}$. Thus $\lambda\in F_{-t}C^\vee$, so $\tau(C^\vee)\le -t$. If $s<-t$, then $-s-1\ge t$ and every functional in $F_sC^\vee$ annihilates $F_tC$, hence pairs trivially with $[x]$. The evaluation pairing identifies $H(C^\vee)$ with $H(C)^\vee$ and is nondegenerate; therefore no such lower filtration level maps nontrivially to total dual homology. This gives $\tau(C^\vee)\ge -t$, and hence $\tau(-K)=-\tau(K)$ in the normalized knot setting.

Choose a smooth embedded arc on $S$ joining its two boundary components. Cut $S$ along a thin strip about that arc, and remove from $S^3\times I$ the interior of a compatible tubular neighborhood of the arc. A properly embedded arc joining the two boundary spheres in this simply connected four-dimensional product is isotopic to a product arc relative its ends: a generic homotopy of such arcs is a path of embeddings, since the coincidence condition for two distinct arc points at the same time has dimension $1+1+1-4<0$, and the derivative-zero condition is also avoidable. These are finitely many compact smooth general-position choices. Removing the product arc neighborhood turns the ambient shell into $B^4$, after rounding its product corners. The cut surface has one boundary component $K_1\#(-K_0)$ and Euler characteristic $\chi(S)+1=1-2g$, hence genus $g$. Its product collars supply the ordinary connected-sum boundary convention. Thus it is an actual smooth genus-$g$ spanning surface for $K_1\#(-K_0)$.

By [F2] and the surface from step 1.2, $$|\tau(K_1\#(-K_0))|\le g_4(K_1\#(-K_0))\le g.$$ Using connected-sum additivity from [F3] and the threshold sign established in step 1.1 gives $\tau(K_1\#(-K_0))=\tau(K_1)-\tau(K_0)$. This proves the stated inequality. If $g=0$, it gives concordance invariance. If one boundary knot is the standard unknot, [F4] gives the four-ball genus estimate; equivalently, puncture an actual spanning surface and use [F5] to obtain that cobordism case. The only external genus assertion used is Hom's direct $\mathbb F_2$ theorem [F2]; no coefficient transfer from the integral surgery-trace maps is made.

Let $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with a regular diagram represented by a valid finite planar code, and let $c$ be its number of crossings. Choose a sufficiently small closed normal tube $N(K)$ and set $E_K=\mathbb R^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$. If $c>0$, there is a subspace $Y\subset E_K$, fixed pointwise by a strong deformation retraction of $E_K$, with a finite relative-open cover
$$Y=U\cup V_1\cup\cdots\cup V_c.$$
The space $U$ deformation retracts to a wedge of $c$ circles. With a common basepoint in the collar above the diagram and access paths in that collar extended into the arc charts, the positive under-arc meridians are its free basis. Each $V_i$ is contractible, $U\cap V_i$ is an open annulus around the $i$-th crossing attachment, and distinct $V_i$ are disjoint. Thus $V_i$ meets $U$ and any previously attached crossing pieces precisely in $U\cap V_i$.

For $c=0$, the Euclidean complement has homotopy type $S^1\vee S^2$, with the circle represented by the positive meridian. In particular its fundamental group is infinite cyclic; the extra sphere at infinity must not be discarded. In all cases the punctured normal tube retracts radially to its boundary, giving a strong deformation retraction $\mathbb R^3\setminus K\to E_K$. These constructions require only finitely many charts and no choice axiom.
For every natural number $n\ge2$, the unit sphere $S^n\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}$ is simply connected ([[def-simply-connected]]).

A topological space $X$ is **simply connected** when it is nonempty and
path-connected ([[def-path-connected]]) and, for every $x_0\in X$, the group
$\pi_1(X,x_0)$ has exactly one element.

Requiring every basepoint avoids presuming a change-of-basepoint theorem. For a
path-connected space that later theorem shows that checking one basepoint is
equivalent, but no such result is needed for this definition. The empty space
is path-connected under the published convention, but it is not simply
connected here because nonemptiness is explicit.

Let $X=U\cup V$, where $U$ and $V$ are open path-connected subsets of $X$, let $U\cap V$ be path-connected, and fix $x_0\in U\cap V$. For the inclusion-induced maps in the diagram

$$\pi_1(U,x_0)\longleftarrow\pi_1(U\cap V,x_0)\longrightarrow\pi_1(V,x_0),$$

the group $\pi_1(X,x_0)$, together with the two inclusion-induced homomorphisms, is a pushout ([[def-pushout-of-group-homomorphisms]]). Equivalently, the canonical homomorphism from any pushout $P$ of the displayed diagram to $\pi_1(X,x_0)$ is an isomorphism. No injectivity of either map from the overlap group is assumed.

Under the hypotheses of [[thm-seifert-van-kampen]], if $U\cap V$ is simply connected, then the inclusion-induced homomorphisms give an isomorphism

$$\pi_1(U,x_0)*\pi_1(V,x_0)\cong\pi_1(X,x_0).$$

Let $f:X\to Y$ be continuous and let $x_0\in X$. Composition sends a loop
$\alpha$ at $x_0$ to the loop $f\circ\alpha$ at $f(x_0)$. Using the loop
classes and fundamental group of [[def-based-loops-and-fundamental-group]],
the proposed
**induced homomorphism** is

$$f_*:\pi_1(X,x_0)\longrightarrow\pi_1(Y,f(x_0)),\qquad f_*([\alpha]):=[f\circ\alpha].$$

The next theorem proves that this value is independent of the representative,
that it is a group homomorphism in the sense of [[def-group-homomorphism]], and
that induced maps respect identities, composition and homotopies that fix the
basepoint.

Let $f:(X,x_0)\to(Y,y_0)$ be a continuous map with $f(x_0)=y_0$. Then

$$f_*([\alpha])=[f\circ\alpha]$$

is a well-defined group homomorphism. For pointed continuous maps,

$$\operatorname{id}_*=\operatorname{id},\qquad (g\circ f)_*=g_*\circ f_*.$$

If $f_0,f_1:(X,x_0)\to(Y,y_0)$ are homotopic through a homotopy that keeps
$x_0$ at $y_0$, then $(f_0)_*=(f_1)_*$.

For every pointed topological space $(X,x_0)$, the product

$$[\alpha][\beta]=[\alpha*\beta]$$

is well defined and makes $\pi_1(X,x_0)$ a group. Its identity is the class of
the constant loop $c_{x_0}$, and $[\alpha]^{-1}=[\bar\alpha]$.

Since $K$ is compact, choose $R>0$ with $K$ and $b$ in the open ball $D=B_R(0)$. Put $U=S^3\setminus(K\cup\{\infty\})=\mathbb R^3\setminus K$ and $V=S^3\setminus\overline D$. $$C_p=\{p+t(k(s)-p):s\in S^1,\ t\ge1\}$$
has three-dimensional outer volume zero: on each of finitely many smooth coordinate intervals of $S^1$ and each bounded interval $1\le t\le n$, the defining map is Lipschitz on a compact rectangle; subdividing into $O(N^2)$ squares of side $1/N$ covers its image by balls of radius $O(1/N)$, whose total three-dimensional volume is $O(1/N)$. If the segment $[p,r]$ met $K$ at $k(s)$, then $r=p+t(k(s)-p)$ for some $t\ge1$, contrary to $r\notin C_p$; similarly $[q,r]$ misses $K$. The broken line from $p$ to $r$ to $q$ lies in $U$.

$$y\longmapsto\left((1-t)+t\frac{\rho}{\|y\|}\right)y$$
is a strong deformation retraction of this punctured ball onto the sphere $S^2_\rho$. The punctured ball is path-connected. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Let $F$ be a compact connected oriented Seifert surface with boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal H=(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,w,z)$ be an admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagram representing $(K,F)$. The associated one-pointed hat chain complex $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is the finite-dimensional chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from the minus complex by setting its basepoint variable to zero; its differential counts index-one disks with zero multiplicity at $w$. Assume for this specified data that the differential is nonincreasing in the Alexander filtration, that the absolute Alexander formula below takes integer values, and that $H(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))\cong\mathbb F_2$. Give a generator $\mathbf x$ its absolute Alexander filtration
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field assigned to $\mathbf x$ by the pointed Morse construction, with its prescribed boundary data near the two basepoints; $c_1$ is the first Chern class of the oriented plane field perpendicular to that vector field. To form the zero-framed surgery, remove a tubular neighborhood of $K$ and glue in a solid torus whose meridian is the longitude induced by $F$. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by deleting a boundary collar of $F$ and capping its longitude by the meridian disk of that solid torus. This is the standard integer normalization, with the one-generator diagram of the standard unknot at filtration zero. The subcomplex $F_s\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is spanned by generators of Alexander filtration at most $s$.

More generally, a finite integer-filtered chain complex is a finite-dimensional chain complex $C$ over $\mathbb F_2$ with subcomplexes $F_sC$ such that $F_sC=0$ for all sufficiently small integers $s$ and $F_sC=C$ for all sufficiently large integers $s$. If $H(C)\cong\mathbb F_2$, define
$$\tau(C):=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z:\operatorname{im}(H(F_sC)\longrightarrow H(C))\ne0\}.$$
For the fixed diagram and surface above, write $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)=\tau(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H),F_*\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))$. Once diagram and surface independence is proved, their common value is the knot invariant $\tau(K)$. Until that comparison is proved, $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)$ denotes only the value for the specified data.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented knot $K$, let $V_K$ be its two-dimensional rational Lee homology with the diagram-independent induced decreasing quantum filtration $F^pV_K$. For a nonzero class $x\in V_K$, define its filtration level by
$$ \ell(x)=\max\{p\in\mathbb Z:x\in F^pV_K\}. $$
Set
$$ s_{\min}(K)=\min_{x\ne0}\ell(x),\qquad s_{\max}(K)=\max_{x\ne0}\ell(x), \qquad s(K)=s_{\max}(K)-1=s_{\min}(K)+1. $$
The equality of the two formulas is part of the definition’s well-definedness, supplied by the rank-two Lee filtration theorem.

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in the standard oriented three-sphere,
$$
|s(K)|\le 2g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K),
$$
where $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surface in the standard four-ball with oriented boundary $K$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a connected compact oriented smoothly properly embedded surface of genus $g$, with product collars and oriented boundary $(-K_0\times\{0\})\sqcup(K_1\times\{1\})$ for oriented knots $K_0,K_1$ in the standard three-sphere. A **finite movie** for $S$ is a finite ordered sequence of regular-level link diagrams whose changes are planar isotopies, oriented Reidemeister moves, births, saddles or deaths. Such a movie defines a map on rational Lee homology that preserves the induced decreasing filtration with degree $\chi(S)=-2g$. The map is an isomorphism; consequently
$$
|s(K_1)-s(K_0)|\le 2g.
$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D_+(T_{2,3},2)$ be the positive-clasped Whitehead double of the right-handed trefoil in the Hedden–Ording twist convention, with companion-annulus framing two. Equivalently, start with the three-crossing positive trefoil blackboard parallel, add one negative full annulus twist, and attach the positive clasp as in the admitted sixteen-crossing code. Then
$$s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2.$$

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its normalized bifiltered complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$. The complex of the reverse mirror $-K$ is filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to the dual complex $C(K)^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}(C(K),\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}])$, with dual differential $d\phi(x)=\phi(\partial x)$ and dual basis elements at negated bifiltration coordinates. There is also a Maslov-graded filtered-chain-homotopy equivalence from $C(K)$ to the complex obtained by exchanging the algebraic and Alexander filtrations. These are distinct symmetries: duality negates both filtration coordinates, while conjugation exchanges them.

derivations.claim: Use the admitted cable/clasp diagram of [[lem-explicit-two-twisted-whitehead-double-has-sixteen-crossing-code]]. Its four-strand cable word is $\sigma_1^{-2}(\sigma_2\sigma_1\sigma_3\sigma_2)^3$, with the separate two-crossing clasp and the admitted wiring. The correction to blackboard framing is $-1$ full twist; the trefoil's blackboard framing is $+3$, giving exactly two full twists relative to the zero longitude. Here is a finite grid admission for this same diagram. Draw its sixteen crossing disks and joining orthogonal arrows, scale by $100$, and rotate the drawing by a quarter turn. At a horizontal overcrossing replace its overarc by the ordered vertices $(-10,0),(2,0),(2,4),(10,4),(10,0)$ and its underarc by $(0,-10),(4,-10),(4,2),(0,2),(0,10)$, reversing either order to retain its directed strand. The sole crossing is now $(2,2)$ with the same signed boundary ports. The six required replacements have disjoint supports. Delete straight subdivisions, separate coincident levels by perturbations smaller than $1/100$, and rank the levels. This gives a $33$-grid with exactly the sixteen original signed crossings. Its saved $986$ exchanges, cyclic cuts and three-corner destabilizations give the following $12$-grid, with zero-based rows: $$O=(4,9,6,1,2,11,0,8,5,3,7,10),\qquad X=(8,2,0,7,10,4,5,3,1,9,11,6).$$ Each exchange has nonalternating endpoint intervals or the permitted shared endpoint; each destabilization has three alternating marks in adjacent rows and columns. These conditions verify the individual isotopies and the displayed endpoint. The directed word is the negative reverse of the input traversal: the negative is the orientation-preserving change of viewing direction $(x,y,h)\mapsto(x,-y,-h)$, while the reverse records the independently chosen component orientation. Thus the actual grid is for the reverse of the oriented knot in the Statement, with its positive clasp and two-full-twist framing retained. citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Let $F$ be a compact connected oriented Seifert surface with boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal H=(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,w,z)$ be an admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagram representing $(K,F)$. The associated one-pointed hat chain complex $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is the finite-dimensional chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from the minus complex by setting its basepoint variable to zero; its differential counts index-one disks with zero multiplicity at $w$. Assume for this specified data that the differential is nonincreasing in the Alexander filtration, that the absolute Alexander formula below takes integer values, and that $H(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))\cong\mathbb F_2$. Give a generator $\mathbf x$ its absolute Alexander filtration
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field assigned to $\mathbf x$ by the pointed Morse construction, with its prescribed boundary data near the two basepoints; $c_1$ is the first Chern class of the oriented plane field perpendicular to that vector field. To form the zero-framed surgery, remove a tubular neighborhood of $K$ and glue in a solid torus whose meridian is the longitude induced by $F$. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by deleting a boundary collar of $F$ and capping its longitude by the meridian disk of that solid torus. This is the standard integer normalization, with the one-generator diagram of the standard unknot at filtration zero. The subcomplex $F_s\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is spanned by generators of Alexander filtration at most $s$.

More generally, a finite integer-filtered chain complex is a finite-dimensional chain complex $C$ over $\mathbb F_2$ with subcomplexes $F_sC$ such that $F_sC=0$ for all sufficiently small integers $s$ and $F_sC=C$ for all sufficiently large integers $s$. If $H(C)\cong\mathbb F_2$, define
$$\tau(C):=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z:\operatorname{im}(H(F_sC)\longrightarrow H(C))\ne0\}.$$
For the fixed diagram and surface above, write $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)=\tau(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H),F_*\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))$. Once diagram and surface independence is proved, their common value is the knot invariant $\tau(K)$. Until that comparison is proved, $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)$ denotes only the value for the specified data.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented knot $K$, let $V_K$ be its two-dimensional rational Lee homology with the diagram-independent induced decreasing quantum filtration $F^pV_K$. For a nonzero class $x\in V_K$, define its filtration level by
$$ \ell(x)=\max\{p\in\mathbb Z:x\in F^pV_K\}. $$
Set
$$ s_{\min}(K)=\min_{x\ne0}\ell(x),\qquad s_{\max}(K)=\max_{x\ne0}\ell(x), \qquad s(K)=s_{\max}(K)-1=s_{\min}(K)+1. $$
The equality of the two formulas is part of the definition’s well-definedness, supplied by the rank-two Lee filtration theorem.

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in the standard oriented three-sphere,
$$
|s(K)|\le 2g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K),
$$
where $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surface in the standard four-ball with oriented boundary $K$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a connected compact oriented smoothly properly embedded surface of genus $g$, with product collars and oriented boundary $(-K_0\times\{0\})\sqcup(K_1\times\{1\})$ for oriented knots $K_0,K_1$ in the standard three-sphere. A **finite movie** for $S$ is a finite ordered sequence of regular-level link diagrams whose changes are planar isotopies, oriented Reidemeister moves, births, saddles or deaths. Such a movie defines a map on rational Lee homology that preserves the induced decreasing filtration with degree $\chi(S)=-2g$. The map is an isomorphism; consequently
$$
|s(K_1)-s(K_0)|\le 2g.
$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D_+(T_{2,3},2)$ be the positive-clasped Whitehead double of the right-handed trefoil in the Hedden–Ording twist convention, with companion-annulus framing two. Equivalently, start with the three-crossing positive trefoil blackboard parallel, add one negative full annulus twist, and attach the positive clasp as in the admitted sixteen-crossing code. Then
$$s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2.$$

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its normalized bifiltered complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$. The complex of the reverse mirror $-K$ is filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to the dual complex $C(K)^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}(C(K),\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}])$, with dual differential $d\phi(x)=\phi(\partial x)$ and dual basis elements at negated bifiltration coordinates. There is also a Maslov-graded filtered-chain-homotopy equivalence from $C(K)$ to the complex obtained by exchanging the algebraic and Alexander filtrations. These are distinct symmetries: duality negates both filtration coordinates, while conjugation exchanges them.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Work in the smooth category ([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Fix once and for all the
three-sphere as the one-point compactification

$$S^3:=\mathbb R^3\cup\{\infty\}$$

of Euclidean three-space, carrying its standard smooth structure, and fix the
standard orientation of $S^3$: the orientation induced by the standard
orientation of $\mathbb R^3$ under the one-point compactification, so that the
charts of the standard atlas away from $\infty$ are orientation-preserving and
the orientation is that of a connected oriented $3$-manifold in the sense of
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]. For $r>0$ write
$\overline B_r:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:\lVert x\rVert_2\le r\}$, the closed ball of
[[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]] with the following restriction convention. Smoothness on a closed ball means
local extension to a smooth map on an open neighborhood in Euclidean space;
smoothness on $M\times I$, for a smooth manifold $M$ without boundary, means
local extension across $t=0,1$ in $M\times\mathbb R$. Thus these closed domains
are not asserted to be manifolds without boundary in the cited definition.

**Links.** The **standard oriented circle** is the circle
$S^1=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ with its standard counterclockwise orientation,
regarded as a smooth $1$-manifold; a
**finite disjoint union of oriented circles** is a smooth manifold
$C=S^1\sqcup\dots\sqcup S^1$ ($k$ summands, $k\in\mathbb N$)
diffeomorphic to the disjoint union of $k$ standard oriented circles. An
**oriented link** (with $k$ components) is a smooth embedding

$$L\colon C\longrightarrow S^3$$

of such a disjoint union in the sense of [[def-smooth-embedding]]. So $L$ is
injective, is an immersion, and is a homeomorphism onto its image with the
subspace topology, and its image $L(C)$ is a finite disjoint union of smoothly
embedded circles. Thus every link considered here is finite and tame: the
smoothness of $L$ is exactly the standing convention, and no polygonal or other
tame model is used. The **components** of $L$ are the images of the individual
summands, and the number of components is $k$.

**Ambient isotopy.** Let $I=[0,1]$. An **ambient isotopy** of $S^3$ is a smooth
map

$$H\colon S^3\times I\longrightarrow S^3$$

such that $H_0=\mathrm{id}_{S^3}$, each $H_t\colon S^3\to S^3$,
$H_t(x):=H(x,t)$, is a diffeomorphism ([[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]]),
and each $H_t$ is orientation-preserving with respect to the fixed orientation.
The last clause is in fact automatic: $t\mapsto H_t$ is continuous in the
$C^\infty$ topology of the diffeomorphism group, the orientation sign is locally
constant in $t$, and $H_0=\mathrm{id}$ is orientation-preserving, so it is kept
only for emphasis.

**Equivalence of links.** Two oriented links $L_0\colon C_0\to S^3$ and
$L_1\colon C_1\to S^3$ are **equivalent** (written $L_0\sim L_1$), or
**ambient isotopic**, when there are an ambient isotopy $H$ and an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism $f:C_0\to C_1$ with
$H_1\circ L_0=L_1\circ f$. Thus parametrizations and component labels are
irrelevant, while the induced orientation of each image component is preserved. The relation is an equivalence relation on links:
it is reflexive with $H=\mathrm{id}$, transitive by composing isotopies, and
symmetric because a smooth family of diffeomorphisms has a smooth family of
inverses. An equivalence class is an **(oriented) link type**.

**Moving off $\infty$.** Because the definition of equivalence allows the
isotopy to move a link through $\infty$, the standard practice of this page is
to first apply an ambient isotopy that carries a given link into the open ball,
and only then to project; every projection and every Reidemeister move below is
read after moving the link off $\infty$ into $\mathbb R^3$ in this way. The
orientation-preserving clause in the definition of ambient isotopy is exactly
what the oriented Reidemeister moves and the oriented closure construction must
respect. The unoriented theory uses the same ambient isotopies but forgets
the orientations of the link components.

**Links in the three-sphere versus links in $\mathbb R^3$.** A link contained in
$\mathbb R^3\subset S^3$ is a link in $S^3$; conversely every link may be
assumed after isotopy to lie in $\mathbb R^3$, by choosing a point outside the compact one-dimensional image and moving that
point to $\infty$ by a smooth rotation of the standard sphere. When comparing
links already in $\mathbb R^3$, an isotopy can also be arranged to avoid
$\infty$ throughout; the track-avoidance argument is given in
[[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]].

Assume countable choice, as required for the smooth normal-bundle structure in the tubular-neighbourhood interface. Let $K:S^1\to S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $\nu(K)=TS^3|_K/TK$ be its quotient normal bundle. Equip $\nu(K)$ with a chosen smooth fibre norm $\|\cdot\|$. Let $\Phi:\Omega\to S^3$ be a tubular-neighbourhood map from an open neighbourhood $\Omega$ of the zero section in $\nu(K)$ that restricts to the inclusion of $K$. For $\epsilon>0$, define the closed disk subbundle
$$
D_\epsilon\nu(K):=\{v\in\nu(K):\|v\|\le\epsilon\}.
$$
Choose $\epsilon$ so that $D_\epsilon\nu(K)\subseteq\Omega$, and set $N(K)=\Phi(D_\epsilon\nu(K))$. The fibre norm, tubular map, and radius are part of the chosen tubular data. The **exterior** of this chosen tube is
$$
E_K:=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}_{S^3}N(K).
$$
Retain its boundary $T_K:=\partial E_K=\partial N(K)$, orient $E_K$ by restriction of the fixed orientation of $S^3$, and orient $T_K$ as the boundary of $E_K$. The choice of tubular map and radius is part of the input to this definition.

For every smooth oriented embedding $K:S^1	o S^3$, let $
u_K=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$ be the quotient normal bundle. Orient its two-dimensional fibres so that a positive tangent to $K$ followed by a positive basis of the normal fibre gives the fixed orientation of $S^3$. Then $
u_K$ admits a smooth orientation-preserving bundle isomorphism $
u_K\cong K	imes\mathbb R^2$.

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $i:S\hookrightarrow M$ be a closed smooth embedded submanifold. Then there are an open neighbourhood $\Omega\subseteq\nu(S)$ of the zero section in the quotient normal bundle and a diffeomorphism $\Phi:\Omega\to U$ onto an open neighbourhood $U$ of $i(S)$ in $M$, with $\Phi(0_p)=i(p)$ for every $p\in S$. Thus $S$ has a tubular neighbourhood in $M$.

Let $i:S\hookrightarrow M$ be a smooth embedding, and suppose its normal bundle
$\nu(S)$ ([[def-normal-and-conormal-bundles-of-an-embedded-submanifold]]) has
been equipped with its standard smooth-vector-bundle structure. Under
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ the existence of this structure is supplied by
[[prop-normal-and-conormal-bundles-are-smooth-vector-bundles]].

A **tubular neighbourhood of $S$ in $M$** consists of:

1. an open neighbourhood $\Omega\subseteq \nu(S)$ of the zero section, and
2. a smooth embedding $\Phi:\Omega\to M$

such that:

- $\Phi(0_p)=i(p)$ for every $p\in S$, and
- $\Phi(\Omega)$ is an open neighbourhood of $i(S)$ in $M$.

Equivalently, $\Phi$ is a diffeomorphism from $\Omega$ onto an ambient open
neighbourhood of $S$, and its restriction to the zero section is the original
inclusion.

derivations.claim: By [F1], $K$ is continuous and $K(S^1)$ is compact because $S^1$ is compact. Since $S^3$ is Hausdorff, $K(S^1)$ is closed; [F1] also identifies it as a smooth embedded submanifold. Thus the closed smooth embedded hypothesis of [F4] holds, and [A1] permits its application. Take a tubular map $\Phi:\Omega\to U\subset S^3$ defined on an open neighbourhood of the zero section of $\nu(K)$.

Use the trivialization [F3] and its product Euclidean norm as the chosen smooth fibre norm in [F2], so $\Omega$ is open in $S^1\times\mathbb R^2$. For each $s\in S^1$, openness gives an arc $I_s$ about $s$ and a radius $r_s>0$ with $I_s\times D^2_{r_s}\subset\Omega$. Compactness of $S^1$ gives a finite subcover by such arcs; taking $\epsilon$ smaller than half the least of their radii yields $S^1\times D^2_{2\epsilon}\subset\Omega$. The closed disk subbundle $S^1\times D^2_\epsilon$ therefore lies in $\Omega$.

Put $N(K)=\Phi(S^1\times D^2_\epsilon)$. The restricted map is a smooth embedding, so $N(K)$ is a compact embedded solid torus with boundary $T_K=\Phi(S^1\times\partial D^2_\epsilon)\cong S^1\times S^1$. Since $S^3$ is compact and $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ is closed, $E_K$ is compact. The annulus $S^1\times\{z:\epsilon/2<|z|<2\epsilon\}$ maps to a collar of $T_K$; in these coordinates $E_K$ is the side $|z|\ge\epsilon$. Thus $E_K$ is a smooth three-manifold with boundary exactly $T_K$, oriented by restriction of the orientation of $S^3$ as in [F2].

On $S^3\setminus K$, define $H_t$ to be the identity outside $N(K)$ and, in the punctured disk fibres with $0<|z|\le\epsilon$, set $H_t(\Phi(s,z))=\Phi(s,((1-t)|z|+t\epsilon)z/|z|)$ for $0\le t\le1$. The formula is continuous for $z\ne0$ and is the identity at $|z|=\epsilon$, so it glues continuously to the identity outside $N(K)$. It fixes every point of $E_K$, stays in $S^3\setminus K$, and at $t=1$ sends every point of the punctured tube to $T_K\subset E_K$. Hence $H_t$ is a strong deformation retraction of $S^3\setminus K$ onto $E_K$.

Use coordinates $(z,t)\in\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ on oriented $\mathbb R^3$, with $t$ increasing upward. A knot is a smooth embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ with the orientation of $S^1$. A strict Morse presentation is one for which $t|_K$ has nondegenerate critical points, meaning its second derivative in a local coordinate is nonzero there, and pairwise distinct critical values. Write $t_{\min}:=\min_{x\in K}t(x)$, $t_{\max}:=\max_{x\in K}t(x)$, and $r(K)$ for the number of local maxima. A parenthesized $q$-braid is a smooth braid with $q$ strands, each strictly increasing in $t$, together with an ordered binary parenthesization of its lower endpoints and an ordered binary parenthesization of its upper endpoints.

For $n\ge0$, a degree-$n$ chord diagram is an oriented circle with $n$ disjoint unordered pairs of distinct points, called chords. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr}}$ be the rational vector space on these diagrams modulo 4T, and let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}$ be its quotient by 1T as well. A 4T relation fixes one chord $pq$ and another chord endpoint $r$, moves the other endpoint of the second chord to just before or after $p$ and just before or after $q$, and takes the alternating sum of those four diagrams. A chord is isolated when it intersects no other chord, where intersection means that chord endpoints alternate around the circle; 1T sets every such diagram to zero. Put $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{fr/un}}_{\mathbb C}:=\prod_{n\ge0}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr/un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C)$, with multiplication induced by connected sum of diagrams and unit the empty diagram. For $q$ ordered upward strands, let $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ be the completion of the associative algebra generated by $t_{ij}=t_{ji}$ for $1\le i<j\le q$, with relations $[t_{ij},t_{kl}]=0$ when $i,j,k,l$ are distinct and $[t_{ij},t_{ik}+t_{jk}]=0$ when $i,j,k$ are distinct. The generator $t_{ij}$ is a horizontal chord joining strands $i$ and $j$; multiplication stacks diagrams from bottom to top.

More generally, a compact strict Morse tangle $T$ is a compact oriented smooth one-dimensional submanifold of $\mathbb C\times[a,b]$, with distinct boundary points on the planes $t=a$ and $t=b$, transverse to those planes, and with nondegenerate interior critical points of height having distinct critical values. A tangle chord diagram is a finite set of unordered pairs of distinct interior points on the oriented tangle skeleton. Its 4T relation is the same local alternating relation as above on the skeleton. The unframed tangle quotient also sets to zero any chord whose endpoints are consecutive in the order along the same skeleton component; for a circle the order is cyclic and for an arc it is linear. The completed degreewise tangle diagram space is denoted $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}(T)$.

The unframed configuration series of a strict Morse presentation $K$ is the formal degreewise series
$$
Z(K):=\sum_{m\ge0}\frac1{(2\pi i)^m}\int_{t_{\min}<t_m<\cdots<t_1<t_{\max}}\ \sum_{P}(-1)^{\downarrow(P)}[D_P]_{\mathrm{un}}\bigwedge_{j=1}^m\frac{dz_j-dz'_j}{z_j-z'_j}\ \in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}.
$$
The ordered simplex is divided into chambers by the critical values of $t|_K$. In each chamber, $P$ ranges over choices, at each level $t_j$, of an unordered pair of distinct points $(z_j,t_j),(z'_j,t_j)$ of $K$. The diagram $D_P$ joins the corresponding preimages on the oriented parameter circle. The integer $\downarrow(P)$ counts endpoints at which $t$ decreases along the orientation of $K$. The differential form is pulled back to the chamber by the selected local branches. The degree-zero term is the empty diagram with coefficient $1$; the displayed integrals are interpreted as improper integrals on each chamber.

For a compact strict Morse tangle $T$, $Z(T)$ is given by the same formula with $T$ in place of $K$, the interval $(a,b)$ in place of $(t_{\min},t_{\max})$, the chord diagrams on the tangle skeleton in place of circle diagrams, and the corresponding unframed tangle quotient in place of $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}$. A parenthesized braid is a special case with no interior critical points.

For a parenthesized braid path $\gamma$ in the configuration space of $q$ distinct complex points, define its Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov (KZ) series by the degreewise iterated-integral holonomy of
$$\Omega_q=\frac1{2\pi i}\sum_{1\le i<j\le q}t_{ij}\,d\log(z_i-z_j).$$
Explicitly, if $\gamma:[0,1]\to\operatorname{Conf}_q(\mathbb C)$ is an ordinary path with noncolliding endpoints, its holonomy is
$$1+\sum_{m\ge1}\int_{0<t_m<\cdots<t_1<1}\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_1)\cdots\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_m).$$
A tangential endpoint is a limiting collision configuration together with a specified nonzero first-order direction of approach for each colliding cluster. When endpoints have such clusters prescribed by the parenthesizations, the holonomy is the constant term after removing the local logarithmic factors $\exp(t_{ij}\log\varepsilon/(2\pi i))$ at each tangential endpoint. A change between the two parenthesizations of three consecutive strands is encoded by the regularized transport $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}$.

For parenthesized braids the KZ holonomy takes values in the framed strand algebra, where only tangled 4T is imposed; passing from a closed framed strand diagram to an unframed knot applies the quotient by isolated-chord 1T. Fix a standard hump $H$ by starting with the two-critical-point unknot and inserting one local birth of a maximum-minimum pair; thus $H$ has two local maxima. The normalized unframed Kontsevich series of $K$ is
$$
I(K):=Z(K)\,Z(H)^{-r(K)}\in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C},
$$
The normalization uses one copy of $Z(H)$ for each local maximum; its degree-zero term is $1$, so its inverse is interpreted in the product completion. This definition makes no assertion that the unnormalized KZ coefficients are rational or that equal Kontsevich series separate knot types.

Near $z=0$, substitute $G_0(z)=f(z)z^a$ with $f(z)=1+\sum_{n\ge1}f_nz^n$. Comparing coefficients in the differential equation gives $(n-\operatorname{ad}_a)f_n=-b\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}f_j$, where $\operatorname{ad}_a(x)=[a,x]$. On the degree-$N$ quotient, $\operatorname{ad}_a$ raises degree and is nilpotent, so $(n-\operatorname{ad}_a)^{-1}=\sum_{s=0}^{N}(\operatorname{ad}_a)^s/n^{s+1}$ is defined. This determines every $f_n$ uniquely. If $S_n=\sum_{j=0}^n\|f_j\|$ in any norm on the finite-dimensional quotient, the recurrence gives $S_n\le(1+C_N/n)S_{n-1}$ for a constant $C_N$; hence $S_n$ grows at most polynomially, and $f$ converges for $|z|<1$. It solves the equation by termwise differentiation.

Replacing $z$ by $1-z$ and interchanging $a,b$ gives the same recurrence at $z=1$ and uniquely constructs $G_1(z)=g(1-z)(1-z)^b$ with $g(0)=1$. The same coefficient recursion, inductively in the specified nested collision tree, gives a unique regularized transport after removing $\rho^{A_S}$.

Both $G_0$ and $G_1$ solve the same left differential equation. Differentiating $G_1^{-1}G_0$ therefore gives zero, so their ratio is constant. For $G_\varepsilon(z)=G_0(z)G_0(\varepsilon)^{-1}$, the endpoint expansions and $G_0(\varepsilon)^{-1}=\varepsilon^{-a}f(\varepsilon)^{-1}$ give
$$\begin{aligned} \varepsilon^{-b}G_\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)\varepsilon^a &=\varepsilon^{-b}f(1-\varepsilon)(1-\varepsilon)^a\varepsilon^{-a}f(\varepsilon)^{-1}\varepsilon^a\\ &=\varepsilon^{-b}g(\varepsilon)\varepsilon^b\,\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}\,\varepsilon^{-a}f(\varepsilon)^{-1}\varepsilon^a, \end{aligned}$$
where the second equality follows from $G_1(1-\varepsilon)\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}=G_0(1-\varepsilon)$. In each degree, $f(\varepsilon)^{-1}-1$ and $g(\varepsilon)-1$ are $O(\varepsilon)$. Since $a$ and $b$ have positive degree, conjugation by $\varepsilon^{\pm a}$ or $\varepsilon^{\pm b}$ is a finite polynomial in $\log\varepsilon$ in the degree-$N$ quotient. Thus both outside factors in the last expression differ from $1$ by $O(\varepsilon(1+|\log\varepsilon|)^N)$ in each degree, which tends to zero; the limit is $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}$.

Let $T_K$ be the one-in one-out tangle obtained by cutting the chosen monotone arc of $K$, and let $Q$ be the fixed one-in one-out tangle that inserts one maximum-minimum pair. By construction, $K=\operatorname{cl}(T_K)$, $H=\operatorname{cl}(Q)$, and $K^+=\operatorname{cl}(Q\circ T_K)$.
